24.s: The NSO is headed by the:
o: Chairperson of the National Statistical Commission
Secretary of the Ministry of Finance
24.x: The NSO is headed by the Chief Statistician of India. The office is described as carrying the rank of Chief Secretary, and the Chief Statistician is also Secretary, MoSPI.
24.tq: Distinguish the executive head of NSO from the advisory statistical commission.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s:
Which of the following is NOT among the functions or outputs associated with the NSO?

1. Compilation of national accounts
2. Compilation of the IIP
3. Compilation of CPI for rural, urban and combined sectors
4. Conduct of field surveys such as PLFS, ASUSE and HCES
5. Formulation of monetary policy

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
24.x: Statements 1 to 4 describe NSO-related functions, including national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys. Formulation of monetary policy is not an NSO function.
24.tq: Find the activity belonging to a different policy authority.

24.s: The Index of Industrial Production data are compiled from how many source agencies?
24.x: IIP data are obtained from 14 source agencies and released on the 28th of each month.
24.tq: Use the exact count associated with the statistical compilation process.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

1. National Accounts Division — GDP, consumption and capital formation
2. Economic Statistics Division — IIP
3. Industrial Statistics Wing, Kolkata — ASI
4. National Statistical Office — National Industrial Classification

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
24.x: All four pairs are correct. The National Accounts Division handles GDP, consumption and capital formation; ESD compiles IIP; the Kolkata wing conducts ASI; and NSO compiles the National Industrial Classification.
24.tq: Match each division or body with its specific statistical output.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s:
Which of the following activities is primarily associated with the old NSSO component of the NSO?

1. Periodic Labour Force Survey
2. Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises
3. Household Consumption Expenditure Survey
4. Preparation of annual National Accounts Statistics

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
24.x: PLFS, ASUSE and HCES are field surveys conducted by the NSS component. Preparation of annual National Accounts Statistics is associated with the National Accounts Division.
24.tq: Separate field-survey functions from national-accounts compilation.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: The National Statistical Commission, established in 2006, consists of:
o: The MoSPI Secretary and the four Chief Statisticians of India
A full-time Chairperson and four full-time members
A part-time Chairperson and two full-time members
A part-time Chairperson and four part-time members
24.x: The NSC consists of a part-time Chairperson and four part-time members. The CEO of NITI Aayog is an ex officio member and the MoSPI Secretary is its Secretary.
24.tq: Test the composition separately from ex officio membership and secretarial roles.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s:
Which of the following statements regarding the National Statistical Commission is correct?

1. The CEO of NITI Aayog is an ex officio member.
2. The Secretary of MoSPI serves as its Secretary.
3. It is the nodal body for statistical standards.

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
24.x: All three statements are correct. The NSC is the nodal body for statistical standards, includes the CEO of NITI Aayog ex officio, and has the MoSPI Secretary as its Secretary.
24.tq: Combine composition, office-holding and institutional role in coded form.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: The Central Statistical Office was formed on 2 May 1951 as the:
24.x: The CSO was formed on 2 May 1951 as the Central Statistical Institute and was merged into the CSO in 1954.
24.tq: Distinguish the original institutional name from its later organisational form.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s:
Which one of the following is correctly matched?

A. NSO — umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys
B. NSC — State Domestic Product compiler
C. ISI — department directly under MoSPI
D. State DES — national-level monetary policy authority
o: NSO — umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys
State DES — national-level monetary policy authority
24.x: The NSO is the umbrella body for national accounts, IIP, CPI and surveys. State DES prepares State Domestic Product and state statistics, while ISI is autonomous under the ISI Act, 1959.
24.tq: Identify the correctly assigned institutional role among swapped bodies.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: The Industrial Statistics Wing located at Kolkata is associated with conducting the:
24.x: The Industrial Statistics Wing at Kolkata conducts the Annual Survey of Industries (ASI).
24.tq: Link the location-specific wing with its survey responsibility.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: Which institution is autonomous under the ISI Act, 1959?
24.x: The Indian Statistical Institute is an autonomous institution under the ISI Act, 1959.
24.tq: Distinguish an autonomous statutory institution from government statistical bodies.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: State Directorates of Economics and Statistics are primarily associated with the preparation of:
o: State Domestic Product and state statistics
National Accounts Statistics and IIP for the Union
The United Nations System of National Accounts
24.x: State DES prepare State Domestic Product and other state-level statistics. National-level accounts and IIP are compiled through the NSO and its divisions.
24.tq: Assign the statistical task according to the level of government.
24.sec: CSO/NSO structure - merger, ministry, divisions

24.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the sequence of national income estimates released by the National Statistical Office?
o: First Advance Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → First, Second and Third Revised Estimates
Second Advance Estimate → First Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → Revised Estimates
First Advance Estimate → Provisional Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Revised Estimates
Provisional Estimate → First Advance Estimate → Second Advance Estimate → Revised Estimates
24.x: The prescribed sequence is First Advance Estimate, Second Advance Estimate, Provisional Estimate and thereafter First, Second and Third Revised Estimates.

o: The last working day of May of the following year
7 June of the same financial year
Early January of the same financial year
End-February of the following financial year
24.x: The First Advance Estimate is released in early January of the same financial year.
24.tq: Use the timing-specific direct-recall approach for release-calendar questions.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: Advance estimates of national income are prepared primarily by using the:
24.x: Advance estimates use the benchmark-indicator method, which projects the relevant aggregates using available indicators.
24.tq: Identify the distinctive methodology associated with advance estimates.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Second Advance Estimate:
1. It is generally released at the end of February.
2. The FY26 Second Advance Estimate in the new series was 7.6%.
3. It is released after the Provisional Estimate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: The Second Advance Estimate is released at the end of February and the FY26 estimate in the new series was 7.6%. It precedes, rather than follows, the Provisional Estimate.
24.tq: Reject the statement that reverses the normal release order.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: With effect from 2026, the date for release of the Provisional Estimate was shifted to:
24.x: The Provisional Estimate, earlier released on the last working day of May, was shifted to 7 June from 2026 after consultation with ACNAS.
24.tq: Test the changed date against the earlier release date.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: The change in the release date of the Provisional Estimate was made after consultation with the:
24.x: The change to 7 June was made after consultation with the Advisory Committee on National Accounts Statistics, referred to as ACNAS.
24.tq: Discriminate between similarly placed statistical abbreviations and identify the advisory body.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: In interpreting an estimate of AP livestock growth, which consideration is most important?
o: Only the initial advance estimate is relevant for all analytical purposes
Revised estimates never alter the sign of reported growth
The estimate stage must be specified because the reported growth may differ between AE and FRE
A provisional estimate is always identical to the First Revised Estimate
24.x: The estimate stage must always be quoted. AP livestock growth was reported as +4.79% at AE but -0.51% at FRE, showing that even the sign may change.
24.tq: Apply the estimate-stage principle to a numerical reporting situation.
24.sec: Release calendar - advance, provisional, revised estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: Which department estimates Gross State Domestic Product in Andhra Pradesh?
o: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation alone
Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh
24.x: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh, estimates GSDP for the State.
24.tq: Use the institutional-authority trap by identifying the agency responsible for State accounts.
24.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: The Directorate of Economics and Statistics, Andhra Pradesh, estimates GSDP in how many sectors?
24.x: DES Andhra Pradesh estimates GSDP in nine sectors.
24.tq: Recall the exact sectoral coverage rather than confusing it with institutional-sector classification.
24.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: The First Advance Estimate of Andhra Pradesh GSDP for 2025-26 at current prices was:
24.x: The 2025-26 First Advance Estimate placed Andhra Pradesh GSDP at Rs 17.62 lakh crore at current prices.
24.tq: Test the reported current-price GSDP figure through direct numerical recall.
24.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

24.s:
Consider the following statements regarding State-level national accounts:
1. The APSES base year is 2011-12.
2. MoSPI's uniform GSVA guideline moves States towards the 2022-23 base.
3. States are required to keep State accounts consistent with national accounts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All three statements are correct. APSES continues to use 2011-12, while the uniform guideline moves States towards 2022-23 and requires consistency with national accounts.
24.tq: Combine the existing State practice with the direction of methodological harmonisation.
24.sec: GSDP estimation - DES AP, sectors, advance estimates  [APPSC]

24.s: Under the 2011-12 national accounts series, the headline measure of value added was:
24.x: The 2011-12 series adopted GVA at basic prices as the headline measure.
24.tq: Discriminate between closely related national-accounting aggregates.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: The MCA-21 database was introduced in the 2011-12 series mainly to estimate the private corporate sector through the:
24.x: The MCA-21 company database represented an enterprise approach and partly replaced the earlier reliance on ASI for the relevant estimation.
24.tq: Link the database with the distinctive estimation approach it represents.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which of the following was a major criticism of the 2011-12 national accounts series?
o: It abandoned GVA as a measure of value added
It showed unusually high manufacturing growth that did not match physical indicators
It used only household survey data for manufacturing
It completely excluded the private corporate sector
24.x: The series was criticised for unusually high manufacturing growth that was inconsistent with physical indicators and for overestimating the private corporate sector.
24.tq: Find the correctly stated criticism among claims that reverse the methodological facts.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which one of the following is NOT included among the new data sources used in the 2022-23 national accounts series?
24.x: GST, PFMS and e-Vahan are specifically listed as new data sources for the 2022-23 series. MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing but is not included in this particular list of new data sources.
24.tq: Find the item that belongs to the continuing methodology rather than the listed new data sources.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which of the following methods was included in the 2022-23 series for extending estimates through quantity-based indicators?
24.x: Volume extrapolation was included among the methodological features of the 2022-23 series.
24.tq: Identify the precise technical term rather than a broad but incorrect estimation description.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which of the following correctly states the revised growth figures for 2023-24 and 2024-25?
o: 2023-24 was revised from 9.2% to 7.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 6.5% to 7.1%
2023-24 was revised from 7.2% to 9.2%, while 2024-25 was revised from 7.1% to 6.5%
Both years were revised downward by 2 percentage points
Both years were revised upward by 0.6 percentage points
24.x: The 2023-24 growth estimate was cut from 9.2% to 7.2%, whereas the 2024-25 estimate was raised from 6.5% to 7.1%.
24.tq: Compare the direction of revision separately for the two financial years.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: The nominal GDP estimate for 2022-23 in the revised series was:
24.x: Nominal GDP for 2022-23 was revised to Rs 261 lakh crore from the earlier Rs 269 lakh crore.
24.tq: Distinguish the revised value from the earlier estimate and from the 2025-26 figures.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the nominal GDP estimates for 2025-26 before and after revision?
o: Rs 345 lakh crore to Rs 357 lakh crore
Rs 357 lakh crore to Rs 345 lakh crore
Rs 261 lakh crore to Rs 269 lakh crore
Rs 269 lakh crore to Rs 261 lakh crore
24.x: The nominal GDP estimate for 2025-26 was revised downward from Rs 357 lakh crore to Rs 345 lakh crore.
24.tq: Read the direction of revision carefully and separate 2025-26 from 2022-23 values.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s:
Consider the following sectoral revisions in the new series:
1. Agriculture was revised upward in the range of 3.8% to 5.9%.
2. Finance, real estate and dwellings were revised upward in the range of 7.8% to 9%.
3. Trade GVA was revised downward by 36%.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
24.x: All four sectoral revisions are correctly stated: agriculture and finance-related activities were revised upward, while trade and road transport were revised downward.
24.tq: Check both the direction and the exact range or percentage for each sector.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which statement regarding organised manufacturing and the unincorporated manufacturing sector is correct?
o: MCA-21 is used only for agriculture, and the unincorporated share is 7.8%.
MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing, while the unincorporated share of manufacturing GVA is 13.9%.
MCA-21 was discontinued, and the unincorporated share is 36%.
ASI alone is used for organised manufacturing, and the unincorporated share is 16.9%.
24.x: MCA-21 continues to be used for organised manufacturing, and the unincorporated sector accounts for 13.9% of manufacturing GVA.
24.tq: Pair the continuing database with the precise unincorporated-sector share.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: In 2011-12, the number of manufacturing companies listed in MCA was approximately:
24.x: The MCA database listed 1,35,802 manufacturing companies in 2011-12, compared with 67,649 corporate factories in ASI.
24.tq: Distinguish the company count in MCA from the factory count in ASI.
24.sec: Base year methodology - 2011-12 changes, 2022-23 changes, criticism  [APPSC]

24.s: Which of the following is the correct set of institutional sectors used in the 2022-23 national accounts series?
o: Government, public corporations, private corporations and households

29.x: Chronic poverty lasts for long periods or is transmitted across generations. Transient or cyclical poverty is temporary and generally arises from shocks, seasons or economic cycles.
29.tq: Use duration as the deciding clue when distinguishing chronic from transient poverty.
29.sec: Types of poverty  [other exams]

29.s: Which one of the following correctly describes transient or cyclical poverty?
o: Poverty measured only by comparison with the median income
Poverty caused temporarily by shocks, seasons or economic cycles
Poverty based solely on an individual's perception
29.x: Transient or cyclical poverty is temporary and may result from shocks, seasonal conditions or economic cycles.
29.tq: Match the type of poverty with its duration and immediate cause.
29.sec: Types of poverty  [other exams]

29.s:
Consider the following statements about poverty measurement and economic development:
1. Absolute poverty is measured by the World Bank poverty line.
2. Relative poverty is widely used in developed economies.
3. Relative poverty is defined exclusively by a fixed calorie norm.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because a fixed consumption or calorie norm is associated with absolute poverty, not relative poverty.
29.tq: Split the fixed-norm concept from the society-comparison concept before selecting the code.
29.sec: Types of poverty  [other exams]

29.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally treated as a social indicator of poverty?
29.x: Illiteracy, lack of safe drinking water, poor health and sanitation, and lack of job opportunities are social indicators of poverty. Size of the house is not included in this group.
29.tq: Find the item outside the established social-indicator group.
29.sec: Social indicators of poverty - odd one out  [other exams]

29.s:
Which of the following is included among the standard-of-living indicators of the Multidimensional Poverty Index?
1. Cooking fuel
2. Sanitation
3. Electricity
4. Bank accounts
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
29.x: Cooking fuel, sanitation, electricity and bank accounts are all included among the stated MPI standard-of-living indicators, along with drinking water, housing and assets.
29.tq: Check whether each item belongs to the multidimensional living-standard list before choosing the complete code.
29.sec: Social indicators of poverty - odd one out  [other exams]

29.s: The Head Count Ratio (HCR) measures the:
o: Share of household expenditure devoted to food
Average distance of the poor from the poverty line
Share of the population living below the poverty line
Additional weight assigned to the poorest among the poor
29.x: HCR measures the incidence of poverty, namely the share of the population below the poverty line. Its formula is HC = Nq/N.
29.tq: Match each poverty measure with its specific dimension: incidence, depth or severity.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: The Poverty Gap Index (PGI) primarily captures the:
o: Share of food in total household expenditure
Depth of poverty or average shortfall from the poverty line
Number of people above the poverty line
29.x: The PGI measures the depth of poverty by calculating the average shortfall from the poverty line, expressed as (1/n) Σ (Z − yi)/Z.
29.tq: Distinguish depth from incidence and severity in the poverty-measure framework.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: Which poverty measure gives greater weight to those furthest below the poverty line?
29.x: The Squared Poverty Gap measures the severity of poverty because the normalized poverty gap is squared, giving greater weight to the poorest.
29.tq: Use the effect of squaring the poverty gap to identify the severity measure.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: The Head Count Ratio, Poverty Gap Index and Squared Poverty Gap belong to the:
29.x: HCR, PGI and the squared poverty gap are measures belonging to the Foster-Greer-Thorbecke (FGT) family.
29.tq: Identify the common methodological family rather than confusing it with related inequality indices.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: If the poor become poorer while the number of poor people remains unchanged, which one of the following measures will remain unchanged?
29.x: The Head Count Ratio depends only on the number or share of people below the poverty line, so it does not change when existing poor people become poorer. The Poverty Gap Index changes with the depth of poverty.
29.tq: Apply the incidence-depth distinction to a change in the condition of existing poor persons.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: Engel's Law states that, as family income rises:
o: The share of income spent on food rises proportionately
All household expenditure shifts to food
The share of income spent on food falls
The absolute amount spent on food always becomes zero
29.x: Engel's Law states that the proportion of family income spent on food declines as family income rises, although the absolute amount spent may still increase.
29.tq: Distinguish the share of expenditure from its absolute amount when applying Engel's Law.
29.sec: Poverty measures - HCR, PGI, squared poverty gap (FGT)

29.s: According to the Tendulkar Committee estimates for 2011-12, the monthly poverty line was fixed at:
o: ₹816 in rural areas and ₹1,000 in urban areas
₹1,000 in rural areas and ₹1,407 in urban areas
₹816 in rural areas and ₹1,407 in urban areas
₹972 in rural areas and ₹1,407 in urban areas
29.x: For 2011-12, the Tendulkar poverty line was ₹816 per month for rural areas and ₹1,000 per month for urban areas, approximately ₹27 and ₹33 per day respectively.
29.tq: Separate the committee-specific figures from the later revised poverty-line values.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: The Rangarajan Committee raised the monthly poverty line for 2014 to:
o: ₹1,407 for rural areas and ₹2,100 for urban areas
₹1,000 for rural areas and ₹1,407 for urban areas
₹972 for rural areas and ₹1,407 for urban areas
₹816 for rural areas and ₹1,000 for urban areas
29.x: Rangarajan fixed the poverty line at ₹972 per month in rural areas and ₹1,407 per month in urban areas, equivalent to approximately ₹32 and ₹47 per day.
29.tq: Use the rural–urban order carefully while distinguishing Rangarajan's revised values from Tendulkar's values.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: Which one of the following correctly matches the poverty-line estimates of the two committees?
o: Tendulkar: ₹816 rural and ₹1,000 urban; Rangarajan: ₹972 rural and ₹1,407 urban
Tendulkar: ₹972 rural and ₹1,407 urban; Rangarajan: ₹1,407 rural and ₹2,100 urban
Tendulkar: ₹816 rural and ₹1,407 urban; Rangarajan: ₹1,000 rural and ₹2,100 urban
Tendulkar: ₹1,000 rural and ₹1,407 urban; Rangarajan: ₹816 rural and ₹972 urban
29.x: The correct values are ₹816 and ₹1,000 under Tendulkar and ₹972 and ₹1,407 under Rangarajan, for rural and urban areas respectively. Assigning ₹972/₹1,407 to Tendulkar and ₹1,407/₹2,100 to Rangarajan is a mix-up.
29.tq: Start with the sure committee–value pair and reject the swapped committee assignments.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Modified Mixed Reference Period (MMRP):
1. It uses a seven-day recall period for some food items.
2. It generally records 10–12 per cent higher consumption.
3. It tends to produce a lower poverty estimate.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: MMRP uses a seven-day recall period for some food items. It gives 10–12 per cent higher recorded consumption and consequently produces a lower poverty estimate.
29.tq: Combine the method, its recall period and its statistical effect before selecting the coded option.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: The Modified Mixed Reference Period was first used in poverty estimation by:
o: The National Sample Survey Office in the 1990s
29.x: The Modified Mixed Reference Period, including a seven-day recall period for some food items, was first used by Rangarajan.
29.tq: Identify the committee associated with the methodological innovation rather than the committee associated with the earlier poverty line.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: Which of the following correctly describes the significance of the Household Consumption Expenditure Surveys (HCES) 2022-23 and 2023-24?
o: They were the first surveys to introduce the Tendulkar poverty line.
They constituted the first full MPCE update in over a decade.
They replaced consumption expenditure with income expenditure as the sole measure.
They provided the first official estimates of urban poverty in India.
29.x: The HCES 2022-23 and 2023-24 surveys provided the first full update of Monthly Per Capita Consumption Expenditure (MPCE) in over a decade.
29.tq: Match the surveys with their precise institutional significance, not with unrelated poverty-line developments.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s:
Consider the following statements about the food share in household consumption expenditure:
1. In urban areas, the food share fell from ₹48 to ₹39 per ₹100.
2. In rural areas, the food share was ₹59 per ₹100.
3. The reported urban food share was higher than the reported rural food share.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: The urban food share fell from ₹48 to ₹39 per ₹100, while the rural food share was ₹59 per ₹100. Therefore, the urban share was not higher than the rural share.
29.tq: Compare the direction of change and the rural–urban levels separately before eliminating the reversed comparison.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: The Reserve Bank of India updated the Rangarajan poverty line using HCES 2022-23 through which method?
o: A fixed consumer-price index without survey weights
29.x: The Reserve Bank of India updated the Rangarajan line with HCES 2022-23 using a PLB-weighted price index.
29.tq: Distinguish the exact price-index method from nearby income, calorie and general price-index formulations.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: Tendulkar-line poverty was estimated at approximately what percentages in 2022-23 and 2023-24 respectively?
29.x: Tendulkar-line poverty was estimated at 4.7 per cent in 2022-23 and 2.3 per cent in 2023-24.
29.tq: Read the years in sequence and avoid reversing the two reported estimates.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: Why have critics questioned subsistence-based poverty lines?
o: They use a multidimensional index instead of consumption expenditure.
They count every person above the threshold as affluent.
They hide vulnerability among people just above the poverty threshold.
They measure only urban consumption and exclude rural consumption.
29.x: Critics argue that subsistence poverty lines can conceal the vulnerability of people who are just above the officially defined threshold.
29.tq: Apply the criticism to the practical consequence of being marginally above a threshold.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: The share of India's population below the World Bank's lower-middle-income poverty line reportedly declined from over 50 per cent to approximately:
29.x: The share below the World Bank's lower-middle-income line fell from over 50 per cent to about 30 per cent.
29.tq: Use the trend and approximate endpoint rather than confusing it with a national poverty-line estimate.
29.sec: Poverty line debates - Tendulkar/Rangarajan, HCES 2022-23

29.s: A UNDP simulation estimated that the West Asia war could change India's poverty rate from 23.9 per cent to 24.2 per cent and push approximately how many people into poverty?
29.x: The simulation estimated an increase in India's poverty rate from 23.9 per cent to 24.2 per cent, potentially pushing about 24.6 lakh people into poverty.
29.tq: Keep the percentage-point change and the absolute number of affected people distinct, especially in lakh and crore units.
29.sec: Universal angles

29.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the poverty measure used in Andhra Pradesh:
1. APSES 2024-25 defines absolute poverty with reference to the World Bank line and the calorie norm.
2. Andhra Pradesh's Head Count Ratio in 2011-12 was 9.20 per cent.
3. India's corresponding Head Count Ratio was 21.92 per cent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
29.x: APSES 2024-25 uses both the World Bank poverty line and the calorie norm for defining absolute poverty. The 2011-12 HCR was 9.20 per cent for Andhra Pradesh and 21.92 per cent for India.
29.tq: Check the definition first and then compare the two stated Head Count Ratios without reversing their jurisdictions.
29.sec: Universal angles

29.s: Which one of the following best represents the contemporary debate on measuring poverty in India?
o: Income, consumption and multidimensional measures are debated, with a move towards the MPI.
The poverty line has been replaced entirely by the urban HCR.
Only income measures are used, since consumption measures are no longer relevant.
Only calorie intake is accepted as a complete measure of poverty.
29.x: The debate includes income-based, consumption-based and multidimensional approaches. The movement towards the Multidimensional Poverty Index (MPI) is part of this broader shift.
29.tq: Identify the inclusive option that captures the competing approaches and the movement towards a multidimensional measure.
29.sec: Universal angles

30.s: Which one of the following bodies was associated with the year 1962 in the history of poverty estimation in India?
o: NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty
Expert Group chaired by D.T. Lakdawala
30.x: The Planning Commission Working Group was associated with poverty estimation in 1962. The Task Force on Minimum Needs was constituted in 1979, while the Lakdawala Expert Group and NITI Aayog Task Force belong to later years.
30.tq: Use the year-body association and eliminate bodies belonging to later periods.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: Who among the following authored the study titled ‘Poverty in India’ published in 1971?
o: Suresh D. Tendulkar and C. Rangarajan
30.x: The 1971 study ‘Poverty in India’ was authored by V.M. Dandekar and N. Rath.
30.tq: Test the author-work association directly.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: The Task Force on Minimum Needs, constituted in 1979, was chaired by:
30.x: The 1979 Task Force on Minimum Needs was chaired by Y.K. Alagh.
30.tq: Match the committee year with its chairperson.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s:
Consider the following committees and groups:
1. Planning Commission Working Group
2. Dandekar-Rath study
3. Task Force on Minimum Needs
4. Tendulkar Expert Group
Which of the following is the correct chronological order?
30.x: The correct sequence is 1962 Working Group, 1971 Dandekar-Rath study, 1979 Task Force on Minimum Needs and 2005 Tendulkar Expert Group.
30.tq: Identify the earliest and latest items first, then arrange the middle items by year.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: The Expert Group chaired by D.T. Lakdawala submitted its report in which year, although it was accepted in 1997?
30.x: The Lakdawala Expert Group submitted its report in 1993, and its recommendations were accepted in 1997.
30.tq: Distinguish the report year from the year of acceptance.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: The NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty, constituted in 2015, was chaired by:
30.x: The 2015 NITI Aayog Task Force on Elimination of Poverty was chaired by Arvind Panagariya.
30.tq: Test the chairperson-task force association.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: Which of the following early poverty estimates is correctly matched?
o: Dadabhai Naoroji — ₹75 per year in 1944 prices
National Planning Committee — ₹15–20 per month in 1938
Bombay Plan — ₹16–35 per capita per year in 1867–68 prices
30.x: The National Planning Committee proposed ₹15–20 per month in 1938. Dadabhai Naoroji’s estimate related to 1867–68 prices, while the Bombay Plan proposed ₹75 per year in 1944.
30.tq: Check each historical estimate against both its year and monetary unit.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: Dadabhai Naoroji’s early poverty estimate was expressed at 1867–68 prices as:
30.x: Dadabhai Naoroji estimated poverty at ₹16–35 per capita per year at 1867–68 prices.
30.tq: Focus on the historical figure and distinguish annual from monthly estimates.
30.sec: Committee → year and chairman, chronological order  [APPSC]

30.s: Which committee used a poverty norm of 2,250 kcal per day for both rural and urban areas?
30.x: The Dandekar-Rath study used 2,250 kcal per day as the nutritional norm for both rural and urban areas.
30.tq: Discriminate between similar calorie-based committee recommendations.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: Which one of the following correctly states the calorie norms associated with the Alagh Task Force?
o: 2,155 kcal for rural and 2,090 kcal for urban areas
2,400 kcal for rural and 2,100 kcal for urban areas
2,100 kcal for rural and 2,400 kcal for urban areas
2,250 kcal for rural and urban areas alike
30.x: The Alagh Task Force prescribed 2,400 kcal per day for rural areas and 2,100 kcal per day for urban areas.
30.tq: Compare the rural and urban values rather than recalling only one figure.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Lakdawala methodology:
1. It retained the calorie basis of poverty estimation.
2. It used State-specific poverty lines.
3. It used CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas.
4. It continued scaling poverty estimates to National Accounts.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
30.x: Statements 1, 2 and 3 are correct. Statement 4 is false because the Lakdawala approach stopped scaling poverty estimates to National Accounts.
30.tq: Find the single incorrect methodological feature among closely related statements.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: Which of the following was a significant change introduced by the Tendulkar methodology?
o: Replacement of MRP by URP for all items
Use of one urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas
Removal of private health expenditure from consumption
30.x: The Tendulkar methodology used one urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas. It moved away from an exclusive calorie anchor, included private health and education expenditure, and used MRP in place of URP.
30.tq: Identify the methodological reform and reject reversed or extreme alternatives.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: Which one of the following is NOT a feature of the Rangarajan poverty estimation methodology?
o: Use of calorie, protein and fat norms
Use of a single urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas
Separate treatment of food and non-food requirements
30.x: The single urban poverty line basket for both rural and urban areas was associated with Tendulkar. Rangarajan used separate food and non-food requirements, nutritional norms and MMRP data.
30.tq: Identify the method belonging to the neighbouring committee.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: The Rangarajan methodology prescribed calorie norms of:
o: 2,400 kcal for rural areas and 2,100 kcal for urban areas
2,155 kcal for rural areas and 2,090 kcal for urban areas
2,250 kcal for rural and urban areas alike
2,090 kcal for rural areas and 2,155 kcal for urban areas
30.x: Rangarajan used 2,155 kcal for rural areas and 2,090 kcal for urban areas, along with protein and fat norms.
30.tq: Separate close numerical values by assigning them to the correct area.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes URP from MRP?
o: URP uses a 30-day recall period for all items, whereas MRP uses 365 days for selected low-frequency items.
URP uses a 365-day recall period for every item, whereas MRP uses 30 days for every item.
MRP is used only for urban poverty estimation.
Both URP and MRP use only annual income data.
30.x: URP uses a 30-day recall period for all items. MRP uses a 365-day recall period for five low-frequency items such as clothing, footwear, durables, education and institutional medical care.
30.tq: Split the two recall-period concepts by comparing their time spans and coverage.
30.sec: Committee → method / basis  [APPSC]

30.s: Under the National Multidimensional Poverty Index, the three dimensions are equally weighted. Which of the following is NOT one of these dimensions?
30.x: The National MPI has three equally weighted dimensions: health, education and standard of living. Employment security is not listed as one of the three dimensions.
30.tq: Find the option outside the stated three-part structure.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: India’s National Multidimensional Poverty Index is estimated by:
o: The Finance Commission in association with the World Bank
NITI Aayog in association with UNDP and OPHI
30.x: India’s National MPI is estimated by NITI Aayog with UNDP and OPHI.
30.tq: Apply the ‘who performs this function?’ method to identify the estimating body.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: Which of the following is a standard-of-living indicator in India’s National MPI?
30.x: Standard-of-living indicators include cooking fuel, sanitation, drinking water, electricity, housing, assets and bank accounts.
30.tq: Classify the indicator under the correct MPI dimension.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: Under the Progress Review 2023 covering NFHS-4 to NFHS-5, India’s multidimensional poverty headcount ratio changed from:
30.x: The headcount ratio declined from 24.85% in 2015–16 to 14.96% in 2019–21 under the Progress Review 2023.
30.tq: Distinguish the report period and pair the figures in the correct direction.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: According to the NITI Discussion Paper of January 2024, approximately how many people exited multidimensional poverty over nine years?
30.x: The paper estimated that 24.82 crore people exited multidimensional poverty over the nine-year period.
30.tq: Separate the national nine-year estimate from the Progress Review and State-wise figures.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: Which State recorded the largest fall in the number of multidimensionally poor people?
30.x: Uttar Pradesh recorded the largest fall, involving 5.94 crore people, followed by Bihar, Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan.
30.tq: Rank the State-wise figures by identifying the largest value.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s:
Arrange the following States in descending order of the fall in the number of multidimensionally poor people:
A. Rajasthan
B. Uttar Pradesh
C. Madhya Pradesh
D. Bihar
30.x: The correct order is Uttar Pradesh (5.94 crore), Bihar (3.77 crore), Madhya Pradesh (2.30 crore) and Rajasthan (1.87 crore).
30.tq: Arrange the items by ranking their numerical values from highest to lowest.
30.sec: National MPI (NITI Aayog)  [APPSC]

30.s: According to the 2011–12 poverty-line estimates, which of the following is correctly matched?
30.x: The Tendulkar urban poverty line was ₹1,000 per month, not ₹1,407. The Rangarajan rural and urban lines were ₹972 and ₹1,407 respectively.
30.tq: Match each committee with the correct rural or urban monthly figure.
30.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

30.s: The Tendulkar poverty line for rural areas in 2011–12 was approximately equivalent to:
30.x: The Tendulkar rural poverty line was ₹816 per month, approximately ₹27 per day.
30.tq: Convert or recognise the monthly and daily equivalents of the same poverty line.
30.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

30.s: Which of the following correctly states the all-India poverty ratio under the Tendulkar estimates for 2011–12?
30.x: The Tendulkar all-India poverty ratio was 21.9%; the rural ratio was 25.7% and the urban ratio was 13.7%.
30.tq: Keep the all-India, rural and urban ratios in their proper columns.
30.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

30.s: The all-India poverty ratio recommended by the Rangarajan methodology for 2011–12 was:
30.x: The Rangarajan methodology estimated the all-India poverty ratio at 29.5% for 2011–12.
30.tq: Distinguish the Rangarajan all-India ratio from the Tendulkar ratios.
30.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

30.s: Which statement regarding the Tendulkar and Rangarajan poverty-line figures is correct?
o: The Rangarajan urban line was lower than the Tendulkar urban line.
The Rangarajan rural and urban lines were ₹972 and ₹1,407 per month respectively.
The Tendulkar rural line was ₹972 per month.
Both committees prescribed identical rural and urban poverty lines.
30.x: The Rangarajan poverty lines were ₹972 per month for rural areas and ₹1,407 per month for urban areas. These were higher than the corresponding Tendulkar lines of ₹816 and ₹1,000.
30.tq: Use reversed-comparison traps to compare both committees’ figures.
30.sec: Rangarajan and Tendulkar poverty lines - figures, ratios for 2011-12  [APPSC]

30.s: N.C. Saxena’s report of August 2009 was primarily concerned with:
o: Preparing the rural BPL Census methodology
30.x: N.C. Saxena’s report, prepared for the Ministry of Rural Development, dealt with the method for the rural BPL Census rather than poverty estimation itself.
30.tq: Separate BPL identification from poverty-line estimation.
30.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

30.s: Which of the following was proposed as an example of automatic inclusion in the rural BPL identification approach associated with N.C. Saxena?
30.x: The proposed automatic-inclusion categories included PVTGs, single-woman-headed households, destitute and homeless households, and bonded labourers. Income-tax payers were examples of automatic exclusion.
30.tq: Distinguish automatic inclusion from automatic exclusion categories.
30.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

30.s: The Planning Commission working group associated with the identification of urban BPL families was chaired by:
30.x: S.R. Hashim headed the Planning Commission working group concerned with identifying urban BPL families.
30.tq: Match the expert with the specific BPL-identification task.
30.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

30.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the relationship between poverty estimation and BPL identification?
o: N.C. Saxena dealt with rural BPL Census methodology, while S.R. Hashim dealt with urban BPL identification.
S.R. Hashim dealt with rural BPL identification, while N.C. Saxena dealt with the Global MPI.
N.C. Saxena’s work estimated the national poverty ratio, while Hashim’s work fixed calorie norms.
Both N.C. Saxena and S.R. Hashim dealt exclusively with National MPI estimation.
30.x: N.C. Saxena’s work concerned the rural BPL Census methodology, whereas S.R. Hashim’s working group addressed identification of urban BPL families.
30.tq: Compare the jurisdiction and purpose of two easily confused expert groups.
30.sec: Abhijit Sen / Saxena / Hashim - BPL identification vs methodology  [APPSC]

30.s: Data for poverty estimation traditionally came from NSS consumer expenditure rounds, which were generally conducted once every:
30.x: NSS consumer expenditure rounds were traditionally conducted every five years. The more recent data sources include HCES 2022–23 and 2023–24.
30.tq: Recall the periodicity of the survey rather than the latest survey years.
30.sec: Data and price indices  [other exams]

30.s: Under the Lakdawala method, poverty lines were updated using which combination of price indices?
o: CPI-AL for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas
WPI for rural areas and CPI-IW for urban areas
GDP deflator for rural areas and WPI for urban areas
CPI-IW for rural areas and CPI-AL for urban areas
30.x: The Lakdawala method used the Consumer Price Index for Agricultural Labourers (CPI-AL) for rural areas and the Consumer Price Index for Industrial Workers (CPI-IW) for urban areas.
30.tq: Avoid reversing the rural and urban price-index assignments.

33.x: Keynes explained unemployment in developed economies mainly through deficiency in effective demand, which is associated with demand-deficient or cyclical unemployment.
33.tq: Associate the economist with the precise explanation rather than a related unemployment type.
33.sec: Cyclical unemployment - cause and business-cycle phase  [APPSC]

33.s: Which one of the following best describes the basic nature of unemployment in India?
o: Predominantly technological and confined to manufacturing
Predominantly structural and long-run in character
Entirely cyclical and confined to recessions
33.x: Indian unemployment is basically structural because the demand for labour falls short of supply over the long run due to several structural factors.
33.tq: Separate the broad national character of unemployment from sector-specific forms.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s: Which combination best explains the structural nature of unemployment in India?
o: Only seasonal rainfall variations and tourism cycles
High labour mobility, labour-intensive production and low population growth
Rapid population growth, labour immobility and a shift towards capital-intensive production
Short job-search periods and temporary workplace transfers
33.x: Rapid population growth, labour immobility and the shift towards capital-intensive production contribute to a long-run shortfall of labour demand relative to supply.
33.tq: Select the option containing the structural causes rather than temporary causes.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s: Which one of the following is NOT a structural cause of unemployment in India identified in the context of the secondary sector?
o: Jobless growth and inadequate focus on MSMEs
Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs
Slow infrastructure and delays in official paperwork
Neglected structural transformation of the secondary sector
33.x: Rapid expansion of labour-intensive manufacturing generating abundant jobs would reduce, rather than cause, structural unemployment. The other factors are identified structural impediments.
33.tq: Find the option that reverses the direction of a stated structural cause.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s:
Consider the following statements regarding unemployment in India:
1. A large agricultural workforce contributes to seasonal and disguised unemployment.
2. Indian unemployment differs from the demand-deficient unemployment emphasised by Keynes for developed economies.
3. Underemployment is also a feature of the Indian labour market.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: All three statements are correct. India has substantial seasonal, disguised and underemployment, while its basic unemployment problem is structural rather than solely Keynesian demand deficiency.
33.tq: Combine the sectoral, theoretical and labour-market dimensions before choosing the code.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s: Which one of the following combinations reflects other causes associated with unemployment in India?
o: A complete shift towards labour-intensive manufacturing and export-led growth
Universal formal employment, high female labour force participation and perfect skill matching
Only temporary job search and absence of capital-intensive sectors
Skill-curriculum mismatch, a predominantly informal workforce and low female labour force participation
33.x: Skill-curriculum mismatch, approximately 90% informal employment and low female labour force participation are among the stated causes. Capital-intensive growth and limited export orientation also contribute to the problem.
33.tq: Choose the option that groups multiple related structural labour-market weaknesses.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s: Growth led mainly by capital-intensive IT and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing is associated with
o: The conversion of cyclical unemployment into frictional unemployment
A source of employment-generation limitations in India
The disappearance of underemployment in rural areas
A reduction in structural unemployment through mass job creation
33.x: Capital-intensive growth in sectors such as IT and finance does not generate employment on the scale of labour-intensive manufacturing, thereby contributing to employment limitations.
33.tq: Apply the labour-intensity distinction to the employment effect of growth.
33.sec: Nature of India's unemployment - predominant type and causes  [other exams]

33.s: Educated unemployment in India is predominantly associated with urban areas mainly because
o: Education automatically causes workers to leave the labour force.
Agricultural work is unavailable in every rural month.
Urban workers are excluded from all formal employment.
Educated persons are unable to find jobs matching their qualifications and industry requirements.
33.x: Educated unemployment is an urban phenomenon in which qualified persons fail to find employment matching their education and the needs of industry.
33.tq: Connect the location of educated unemployment with the qualification-job mismatch.

33.s: According to the India Skills Report 2024 figure cited, approximately what proportion of graduates was considered employable?
33.x: The cited India Skills Report 2024 estimate places the employability of graduates at approximately 46%.
33.tq: Retain the precise percentage instead of substituting a rounded majority figure.

33.s: According to PLFS 2025, the unemployment rate for persons with secondary schooling and above was
33.x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure for persons with secondary schooling and above was 6.5%, more than double the national rate.
33.tq: Use the exact education-linked unemployment figure and compare nearby alternatives.

33.s: For persons with secondary schooling and above, the PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was reported as
o: Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 5.9%, respectively
Equal in rural and urban areas, at 6.5% each
Higher in rural areas than in urban areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
Higher in urban areas than in rural areas, at 7.2% and 6%, respectively
33.x: The cited PLFS 2025 rates were 7.2% in urban areas and 6% in rural areas for persons with secondary schooling and above.
33.tq: Compare both the direction and the values of the rural-urban figures.

33.s: Which one of the following correctly states the cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rates for youth aged 18–29 and for tertiary-educated youth, respectively?
33.x: The cited PLFS 2025 unemployment rate was 14.8% for youth aged 18–29 and rose to 29.4% for tertiary-educated youth.
33.tq: Keep the population groups separate when comparing closely related percentages.

33.s: What proportion of tertiary-educated youth was reported to be NEET in PLFS 2025?
33.x: The cited PLFS 2025 figure was 40.1% of tertiary-educated youth being NEET, meaning not in employment, education or training.
33.tq: Distinguish the NEET percentage from the unemployment percentages for the same broad group.

33.s: Which of the following correctly represents the cited unemployment rates among Gen Z graduates?
33.x: The cited figures for Gen Z graduates were 29% for males and 36.9% for females.
33.tq: Check the gender labels before comparing the two percentages.

33.s: The unemployment rate cited for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was
33.x: The cited unemployment rate for Gen Z persons aged 15–26 was 11.9%.
33.tq: Match the age group with its own rate rather than using the youth aggregate figure.

33.s: A person working fewer than the normal number of hours is an example of
33.x: Visible underemployment involves working fewer than normal hours. It can be observed directly from the amount of work performed.
33.tq: Use the observable-hours distinction to separate visible from invisible underemployment.

33.s: An MBA graduate working full-time as a driver at a very low income is an example of
33.x: Invisible underemployment exists when a person works full-time but earns very little or works below their ability, as in the example of an MBA working as a driver.
33.tq: Look beyond the number of hours and identify underutilisation of skills or income.

33.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes frictional unemployment from structural unemployment?
o: Frictional unemployment requires structural reform, whereas structural unemployment ends with a short job search.
Frictional unemployment exists only during depression, whereas structural unemployment disappears during recession.
Frictional unemployment is short-term job-search unemployment, whereas structural unemployment is long-term skill-job mismatch.
Frictional unemployment is caused by technology, whereas structural unemployment is caused by seasonal agriculture.
33.x: Frictional unemployment results from the temporary time lag involved in changing or searching for jobs, while structural unemployment is long-term and arises from a mismatch between skills and available jobs.
33.tq: Separate the two types using cause and duration together.

33.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Frictional unemployment can exist even when the economy is at full employment.
2. Structural unemployment is deep-rooted and may require reskilling or structural reform.
3. Frictional unemployment is generally permanent.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because frictional unemployment is normally short-term and temporary.
33.tq: Use the duration and policy-response contrast to reject the reversed statement.

33.s: A worker voluntarily leaves a job and spends a short period searching for a better one. This is an example of
33.x: The temporary gap caused by quitting one job and searching for another is frictional or search unemployment.
33.tq: Identify the unemployment type from the worker's transition between jobs.

33.s: Which situation best illustrates structural unemployment?
o: A firm laying off workers during a recession
A worker changing jobs after voluntarily quitting
A farm worker remaining idle during the agricultural off-season
A labour-intensive economy shifting towards capital-intensive production
33.x: A shift from labour-intensive to capital-intensive production changes the demand for labour and creates a long-term structural mismatch.
33.tq: Match the example to long-term structural change rather than a temporary interruption.

33.s: Which of the following is correctly matched?
o: Frictional unemployment — needs immediate structural reform
Frictional unemployment — normal even at full employment
Structural unemployment — exists only during economic boom
33.x: Frictional unemployment is a normal feature that can exist even at full employment. Structural unemployment is long-run and deep-rooted, not a temporary search gap or a boom-only phenomenon.
33.tq: Find the correctly matched pair after rejecting reversed definitions and durations.

33.s: A person who is able and willing to work but does not get any job is experiencing which type of unemployment?
33.x: Open unemployment exists when a person is willing and able to work but has no job at all.
33.tq: Distinguish the direct definition from closely related classifications.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: Which one of the following best describes hidden or disguised unemployment?
o: Workers are temporarily dismissed during a recession
Workers refuse jobs because the prevailing wage is low
Persons appear to be employed but make no effective contribution to output
Workers change jobs while searching for a better match
33.x: In hidden or disguised unemployment, persons appear to be employed, but their removal does not reduce output because they contribute nothing or very little to production.
33.tq: Separate apparent employment from actual productive contribution.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s:
Consider the following statements regarding voluntary and involuntary unemployment:
1. Voluntary unemployment occurs when a person is unwilling to work at the prevailing wage.
2. Involuntary unemployment occurs when a person is willing to work at the prevailing wage but cannot find a job.
3. The labour force counts only voluntary unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The labour force counts involuntary unemployment, not only voluntary unemployment.
33.tq: Find the statement that reverses the voluntary–involuntary distinction.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s:
Which of the following may lead to voluntary unemployment?
1. High benefits that reduce the incentive to accept work
2. A high marginal tax rate
3. Waiting for a better-suited job
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
33.x: High benefits, a high marginal tax rate and waiting for a better-suited job are all stated causes of voluntary unemployment.
33.tq: Use the all-inclusive option when each listed cause belongs to the same category.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: Unemployment that persists over a long period is generally classified as:
33.x: Chronic unemployment is long-term unemployment that persists over an extended period.
33.tq: Match the duration-based description with the exact term.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Unemployment trap — unemployment caused by seasonal agricultural activity
Casual unemployment — unemployment lasting for more than twelve months
Long-term unemployment — unemployment arising only from a temporary recession
Classical unemployment — unemployment caused by wages being too high
33.x: Classical, or real-wage, unemployment occurs when wages are too high. Long-term unemployment refers to unemployment exceeding twelve months, while casual unemployment involves day-to-day contract work and an unemployment trap may arise when benefits discourage work.
33.tq: Check the exact cause attached to each similar unemployment term.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: A worker employed on a day-to-day contract basis is most appropriately associated with:
33.x: Casual employment is based on day-to-day contract work; the classification is distinct from chronic and classical unemployment.
33.tq: Apply the employment arrangement rather than the duration or wage condition.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: A person who has remained unemployed for more than 12 months falls under which category?
33.x: Long-term unemployment is defined here as unemployment lasting for more than twelve months.
33.tq: Use the stated time threshold to identify the classification.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: Which situation illustrates an unemployment trap?
o: Benefits discourage a person from accepting available work
Automation replaces a routine manufacturing task
A worker changes jobs while searching for a better match
A recession reduces aggregate demand for labour
33.x: An unemployment trap occurs when benefits reduce the incentive to work and discourage acceptance of available employment.
33.tq: Identify the classification from its behavioural mechanism.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s:
With reference to full employment, consider the following statements:
1. Every person willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work.
2. Full employment implies that frictional unemployment cannot exist.
3. Structural unemployment may still exist at full employment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: Full employment means that everyone willing to work at the prevailing wage finds work, but frictional and structural unemployment may still exist.
33.tq: Reject the absolute claim that full employment eliminates every form of unemployment.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: The natural rate of unemployment is composed of:
33.x: The natural rate is the combination of frictional and structural unemployment existing at full employment.
33.tq: Recall the exact components of a standard composite concept.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is particularly associated with:
33.x: The concept of the natural rate of unemployment is associated with Milton Friedman.
33.tq: Link the named economist with the specific concept rather than a related curve or law.
33.sec: Other classifications - open vs hidden, voluntary vs involuntary, natural rate

33.s: Technological unemployment is best understood as:
o: Job loss caused exclusively by a fall in aggregate demand
Unemployment caused by a worker voluntarily rejecting the prevailing wage
Temporary unemployment during the agricultural off-season
Job loss caused by changes in technology and treated as a subtype of structural unemployment
33.x: Technological unemployment results from technological change and is a subtype of structural unemployment.
33.tq: Use the cause-and-classification link to distinguish technological from cyclical unemployment.

33.s:
Which of the following correctly describes the likely labour-market effect of automation and artificial intelligence?
1. Automation in manufacturing may reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs.
2. Artificial intelligence in services may reduce demand for routine jobs.
3. Technological change can generate structural unemployment.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
33.x: Automation in manufacturing and AI in services can reduce demand for low-skilled and routine jobs, and the resulting technological unemployment is structural in character.
33.tq: Combine the sector-specific examples with their common structural effect.

33.s: Jobless growth is more likely when economic growth is driven mainly by:
o: Labour-intensive manufacturing rather than capital-intensive activities
Capital-intensive sectors such as information technology and finance rather than labour-intensive manufacturing
33.x: Growth led by capital-intensive sectors such as IT and finance, instead of labour-intensive manufacturing, can produce jobless growth.
33.tq: Focus on the reversed capital-intensive versus labour-intensive comparison.

33.s: The Phillips curve was named after A.W. Phillips, whose relevant work dates to:
33.x: The Phillips curve is named after A.W. Phillips and is associated with his 1958 work.
33.tq: Use the date-specific option rather than confusing it with later developments of the theory.

33.s: The traditional trade-off between inflation and unemployment breaks down in a situation of:
o: Stable prices with potential output growth
Stagflation, characterised by high inflation and high unemployment
33.x: Stagflation combines high inflation with high unemployment and therefore breaks down the traditional Phillips-curve trade-off.
33.tq: Identify the unusual combination that contradicts the traditional inverse relationship.

33.s:
Consider the following statements about the long-run Phillips curve:
1. It is vertical at the natural rate of unemployment.
2. The long-run formulation is associated with Friedman and Phelps.
3. It establishes a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
33.x: The long-run Phillips curve is vertical at the natural rate and is associated with Friedman and Phelps. It does not establish a permanent trade-off between inflation and unemployment.
33.tq: Separate the short-run trade-off from the long-run vertical-curve proposition.

33.s: According to Okun's law, a one percentage point rise in unemployment above the natural rate is associated approximately with:
o: A 2% rise in output above potential GDP
A 1% rise in output above potential GDP
A 2% fall in output below potential GDP
A 5% fall in output below potential GDP
33.x: Okun's law states that a one percentage point increase in unemployment above the natural rate is associated with roughly a 2% reduction in output below potential GDP.
33.tq: Track both parts of the quantitative relationship: the unemployment point and the output percentage.

33.s: Okun's law is associated with:
33.x: The inverse relationship between unemployment and the gap between actual and potential output is known as Okun's law, associated with Arthur Okun.
33.tq: Match the economic law with its principal economist.

33.s: According to the monthly PLFS data cited for May 2026, India's unemployment rate was:
33.x: The monthly PLFS unemployment rate rose to 5.5% in May 2026 from 5.2% in April 2026.
33.tq: Distinguish the current-month value from the immediately preceding month and other comparative figures.

33.s: Which one of the following correctly presents the monthly PLFS unemployment-rate movement cited for India?
o: It rose from 3.2% in April 2026 to 4.1% in May 2026.
It declined from 5.5% in April 2026 to 5.2% in May 2026.
It remained unchanged at 5.2% during April and May 2026.
It rose from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
33.x: The unemployment rate increased from 5.2% in April 2026 to 5.5% in May 2026.
33.tq: Check the direction of change as well as the two month-specific figures.

33.s: For May 2026, the rural and urban unemployment rates cited for India were respectively:
33.x: The cited May 2026 rates were 5.1% for rural areas and 6.4% for urban areas.
33.tq: Preserve the order of the paired rural and urban figures.

33.s: Which statement regarding seasonal labour migration is correct?
o: Nearly 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 3–5 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
More than 100 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
Nearly 10–15 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
33.x: Approximately 30–35 million seasonal labourers migrate annually.
33.tq: Identify the stated range rather than selecting a nearby but incorrect magnitude.

33.s: The unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh, compared with the all-India rate cited for the PLFS 2023–24 and APSES 2024–25 comparison, was:
33.x: Andhra Pradesh recorded 4.1% unemployment compared with 3.2% for India, making the AP rate higher by 0.9 percentage points.
33.tq: Subtract the paired rates and retain the direction of the comparison.

33.s:
Which of the following correctly states the unemployment indicators for Andhra Pradesh cited in the comparison?
1. Overall unemployment rate in Andhra Pradesh was 4.1%.
2. Youth unemployment rate for the 15–29 age group was 17.5%.
3. Urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
33.x: All three figures are correct: overall unemployment was 4.1%, youth unemployment for ages 15–29 was 17.5%, and urban female youth unemployment was 29.1%.
33.tq: Use the all-inclusive option after verifying each age- and gender-specific figure.

33.s: In the overall gender-wise unemployment figures cited for Andhra Pradesh, which comparison is correct?
o: Female and male unemployment were both 4.1%.
Female unemployment was 29.1% and male unemployment was 17.5%.
Female unemployment was 3.7% and male unemployment was 4.3%.
Female unemployment was 4.3% and male unemployment was 3.7%.
33.x: The cited overall figures were 3.7% for females and 4.3% for males.
33.tq: Avoid reversing the two gender-specific values.

33.s: A decline in the measured unemployment rate may fail to indicate genuine job creation when it results from:
o: A rise in potential GDP caused by technology
A permanent reduction in the labour force due to higher wages
33.x: A falling unemployment rate may reflect people entering low-productivity work under distress rather than the creation of good or adequate jobs.
33.tq: Distinguish an apparently favourable indicator from its possible underlying labour-market condition.

33.s: Which of the following comparisons between India and developed countries is correct?
o: India mainly faces cyclical unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face disguised unemployment.
Developed countries mainly face seasonal unemployment, whereas India mainly faces classical unemployment.
India mainly faces structural and disguised unemployment, whereas developed countries mainly face cyclical, demand-deficient unemployment.
Both India and developed countries mainly face only frictional unemployment.
33.x: India's unemployment is characterised as structural and disguised, while developed countries are described as facing mainly cyclical or demand-deficient unemployment.
33.tq: Keep both sides of the comparative classification aligned with the stated economic context.

33.s: Which economist is associated with the explanation of cyclical unemployment in developed countries as demand-deficient unemployment?
33.x: The demand-deficiency explanation of cyclical unemployment is associated with Keynes.
33.tq: Match the explanatory framework with the economist associated with it.

34.s: Under the Usual Principal Status approach, a person is treated as employed when the person has worked for the major part of the reference period. What is the relevant reference period and minimum duration?
o: Each day and 4 hours of work
34.x: UPS uses a reference period of 365 days. A person is considered employed if the major part of the year, generally 183 days or more, was spent working.
34.tq: Match the reference period with the qualifying duration.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Usual Principal and Subsidiary Status approach?
o: It counts only persons working for 183 days or more in a year.
It counts a person as employed if work was performed for four hours on any day.
It includes principal-status workers and those undertaking subsidiary work for at least 30 days in the year.
It counts a person as employed only if work was performed on each day of the reference week.
34.x: UPSS includes persons employed under principal status as well as those who performed subsidiary work for at least 30 days during the 365-day reference period.
34.tq: Discriminate between principal-status and subsidiary-status conditions.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: In the Current Daily Status approach, the basic time unit used for recording employment is:
34.x: CDS uses a half-day as the unit of measurement. Four or more hours of work are treated as employment for that day.
34.tq: Test the precise quantitative unit used in a statistical approach.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: A person worked for five hours on one day and remained without work on the other days of the reference week. Under which approach would the person be treated as employed for that day?
34.x: Under CDS, four or more hours of work count as employment for the day. The approach records employment and unemployment for each day of the seven-day period.
34.tq: Apply the qualifying-hour rule to a short employment situation.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: Why does the Current Daily Status approach generally produce the highest unemployment rate?
o: It counts days of unemployment even for persons treated as employed under CWS.
It uses a reference period of 365 days.
It includes only persons who are not seeking work.
It excludes all seasonal workers from employment.
34.x: CDS records unemployment separately for each day and therefore captures intermittent unemployment that may not be reflected when a person is counted as employed under CWS.
34.tq: Identify the cause behind a comparison in measured unemployment rates.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: Which one of the following is NOT an unemployment measurement approach used in the listed status-based framework?
34.x: Current Monthly Status is not one of the listed NSS status approaches. UPS, CWS and CDS are recognised approaches in this framework.
34.tq: Find the non-method inserted among closely related statistical methods.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: In Census terminology, which combination is correctly matched?
o: Main worker — worked for less than 183 days in a year
Marginal worker — worked for 183 days or more in a year
Main worker — worked for 183 days or more in a year
Main worker — worked only for one hour during the reference week
34.x: The Census classifies a person who worked for 183 days or more in a year as a main worker. A person working for less than 183 days is a marginal worker.
34.tq: Separate Census worker categories from NSS status approaches.
34.sec: Status approaches - UPS, UPSS, CWS, CDS  [APPSC]

34.s: The unemployment rates under UPS, CWS and CDS in the NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 were respectively:
34.x: For 2011–12, the NSS 68th Round reported unemployment rates of 2.7% under UPS, 3.7% under CWS and 5.6% under CDS.
34.tq: Recall the ordered numerical series and preserve the approach sequence.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: Which of the following was the last quinquennial round of the National Sample Survey relating to employment and unemployment?
34.x: The NSS 68th Round for 2011–12 was the last quinquennial employment-unemployment round before the PLFS system became the regular source of such estimates.
34.tq: Identify the terminal item in a sequence of survey rounds.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: The unemployment rate for persons aged 15 years and above in the first PLFS, conducted for 2017–18, was:
34.x: The first PLFS, for 2017–18, reported an unemployment rate of 6.1% for persons aged 15 years and above.
34.tq: Link the first survey year with its reported headline rate.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
34.x: PLFS 2022–23 reported an overall unemployment rate of 3.2%, while the rate for graduates was 13%. The other year-rate combinations are incorrect.
34.tq: Match each survey year with its distinctive rate or finding.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s:
Consider the following statements about PLFS 2023–24:
1. The overall unemployment rate under UPSS was 3.2%.
2. The rural unemployment rate was lower than the urban rate.
3. The urban unemployment rate was 5.1%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
34.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The urban rate was 5.1%, while the rural rate was 2.5%, so statement 3 is false.
34.tq: Compare the overall, rural and urban figures before selecting the code.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: Which of the following correctly represents the monthly CWS unemployment rates for March, April and May 2026, respectively?
34.x: The monthly CWS rates were 5.1% in March 2026, 5.2% in April 2026 and 5.5% in May 2026.
34.tq: Preserve the chronological order of closely spaced monthly figures.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: The quarterly CWS unemployment rate for January–March 2026, along with the urban and rural rates, was:
34.x: For January–March 2026, the quarterly CWS unemployment rate was 5.0%; the urban rate was 6.6% and the rural rate was 4.3%.
34.tq: Match the aggregate figure with its two geographical components.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: As reported by CMIE, approximately how many persons were unemployed in India in December 2021?
34.x: CMIE reported approximately 53 million unemployed persons as of December 2021.
34.tq: Recall the distinctive large-scale numerical estimate associated with a private agency.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: Which statement correctly distinguishes the CMIE estimate from official PLFS figures?
o: CMIE conducts the quinquennial NSS employment-unemployment rounds.
CMIE reports only decennial Census worker data.
CMIE is a private source and its unemployment rate was about 7.95% in September 2023, higher than the official PLFS figures.
CMIE is a government survey and generally reports lower unemployment than PLFS.
34.x: CMIE is a private source. Its unemployment rate was approximately 7.95% in September 2023, higher than the corresponding official PLFS figures.
34.tq: Separate private and official sources using agency and trend clues.
34.sec: Unemployment rate figures - PLFS and NSS rounds  [APPSC]

34.s: The Periodic Labour Force Survey is conducted by:
o: The Census of India under the Ministry of Home Affairs
The National Statistical Office under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
The Centre for Monitoring Indian Economy under NITI Aayog
