73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Gross terms of trade — export price index/import price index
Income terms of trade — import quantity/export quantity
Gross terms of trade — import quantity index/export quantity index
Net terms of trade — import quantity index/export quantity index
73.x: Gross terms of trade is defined as the import quantity index divided by the export quantity index. NTT uses price indices, while ITT is NTT multiplied by the export quantity index.
73.tq: Start with the sure distinction between price-based NTT and quantity-based GTT.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: A country has an absolute advantage in producing a commodity when it:
o: Produces it at a lower absolute cost than other countries
Produces it at a lower opportunity cost than every other commodity
Exports it below its home-market price
Restricts imports through a quantitative ceiling
73.x: According to Adam Smith's concept, absolute advantage means producing a good at a lower absolute cost than others.
73.tq: Discriminate between absolute cost and opportunity cost.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Comparative advantage requires a country to specialise in producing the good with the:
73.x: Ricardo's theory of comparative advantage focuses on specialising in the good with the lower opportunity cost.
73.tq: Use the defining keyword opportunity cost to identify comparative advantage.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Export promotion and import substitution are respectively described as:
73.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy, whereas export promotion is an outward-looking strategy.
73.tq: Test the paired terms by reversing them mentally and checking their policy orientation.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Dumping occurs when a firm:
o: Imports goods only under a tariff quota
Exports a product at a price below its home-market price or cost
Receives a domestic subsidy for exports
73.x: Dumping means exporting a product at a price below its home-market price or below its cost. It may attract anti-dumping duties.
73.tq: Distinguish the pricing practice of dumping from subsidies and re-exporting.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: Rules of origin — fix the international price of exports
Anti-dumping duty — offsets foreign government subsidies
Countervailing duty — responds to dumped imports below home-market price
Countervailing duty — offsets the effect of foreign subsidies
73.x: Countervailing duty offsets the effect of foreign subsidies. Anti-dumping duty addresses imports sold below home-market price or cost, while rules of origin determine the national source of goods.
73.tq: Separate the remedies for dumping and foreign subsidies before eliminating the mismatched pairs.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: The principal purpose of rules of origin is to determine:
o: The international price of a product
The amount of countervailing duty payable
The national source of a product
73.x: Rules of origin establish the national source of a product and help determine eligibility for free-trade agreement concessions.
73.tq: Identify the administrative question answered by the rule rather than its possible trade consequence.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: Autarky refers to a state of:
o: Economic self-sufficiency with minimal external trade
73.x: Autarky is a condition of economic self-sufficiency in which an economy has little or no dependence on external trade.
73.tq: Use the contrast between self-sufficiency and external trade to identify the term.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s: India's share in world merchandise exports changed from 2.2% in 1948 to approximately what level in 1983?
73.x: India's share in world merchandise exports declined from 2.2% in 1948 to 0.5% in 1983.
73.tq: Read the historical trend from the stated starting and ending years.
73.sec: India's share in world merchandise exports - trend and rank

73.s: Which of the following correctly represents India's share in world trade exports in the stated years?
73.x: India's share in world trade declined from 1.78% in 1950 to 0.6% in 1995.
73.tq: Check both the year and the direction of change rather than memorising the percentages alone.
73.sec: India's share in world merchandise exports - trend and rank

73.s: India's share in world merchandise exports increased from 1% in 2005 to what percentage in 2024?
73.x: India's share in world merchandise exports rose from 1% in 2005 to 1.8% in 2024.
73.tq: Distinguish the export share of 1.8% from the import share of 2.8%.
73.sec: India's share in world merchandise exports - trend and rank

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India's merchandise trade in 2024:
1. India ranked 18th among world merchandise exporters.
2. India's share in world merchandise exports was 1.8%.
3. India ranked ninth among world merchandise importers.
4. India's share in world merchandise imports was 2.8%.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All four statements correctly describe India's merchandise export and import position in 2024.
73.tq: Pair each rank with its corresponding share before choosing the complete combination.
73.sec: India's share in world merchandise exports - trend and rank

73.s: The services surplus in FY25 reached approximately:
73.x: India's services surplus reached a record $188.8 billion in FY25.
73.tq: Separate the services surplus from the merchandise deficit and quarterly deficit figures.
73.sec: India's share in world merchandise exports - trend and rank

73.s: Which one of the following correctly describes India's external trade position in August 2026?
o: Total exports were $45.2 billion, imports were $70.7 billion and the deficit was $25.5 billion
Total exports were $92.1 billion, imports were $82.7 billion and the surplus was $9.4 billion
Total exports were $82.7 billion, imports were $92.1 billion and the deficit was $9.4 billion
Goods exports were $43.8 billion, imports were $45.2 billion and the deficit was $11.6 billion
73.x: In August 2026, total exports were $82.7 billion, imports were $92.1 billion and the deficit declined to $9.4 billion from $11.6 billion.
73.tq: Keep total trade figures separate from goods-only figures reported for the same period.
73.sec: Trade deficit - merchandise vs services, causes, record

73.s: Which development was reported for India's merchandise exports in August 2026?
o: They increased by 26.1% to $43.8 billion, growing more than imports in absolute terms for the first time
73.x: Merchandise exports grew by 26.1% to $43.8 billion in August 2026 and, for the first time, grew more than imports in absolute terms.
73.tq: Combine the direction, rate and value of change without confusing them with May's record.
73.sec: Trade deficit - merchandise vs services, causes, record

73.s: Which of the following was reported as a record level of goods exports in May 2026?
73.x: Goods exports reached a record $45.2 billion in May 2026.
73.tq: Match the month-specific record with its exact value, avoiding the August figure.
73.sec: Trade deficit - merchandise vs services, causes, record

73.s: The principal merchandise export ports of Andhra Pradesh include:
o: Visakhapatnam as a major port and Krishnapatnam and Kakinada as non-major ports
Krishnapatnam as the only major port and Visakhapatnam as a non-major port
Kakinada and Nellore as major ports only
Vijayawada, Guntur and Tirupati as major ports
73.x: Visakhapatnam is a major port, while Krishnapatnam and Kakinada are identified as non-major ports of Andhra Pradesh.
73.tq: Classify the ports by status and reject options that change their locations or categories.
73.sec: AP exports - items, ports, share

73.s: Approximately what share of India's shrimp exports is associated with Andhra Pradesh?
73.x: Andhra Pradesh accounts for about 70% of India's shrimp exports, particularly white-leg shrimp produced in West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore.
73.tq: Distinguish the State's national export share from its production districts and products.
73.sec: AP exports - items, ports, share

73.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Andhra Pradesh's export strengths?
o: Kurnool — petroleum products from a refinery
73.x: Petroleum products are associated with the Visakhapatnam refinery, not Kurnool. Guntur is known for chillies, while West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore are associated with white-leg shrimp.
73.tq: Find the wrong location-product pair using the nearby regional associations.
73.sec: AP exports - items, ports, share

73.s: Which combination represents export-related strengths of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Chillies, turmeric, mango pulp, pharmaceuticals and petroleum products
Tea, coffee, wool, automobiles and crude oil
Coal, jute, iron ore, silk and natural gas
Cotton yarn, sugarcane, bauxite and shipbuilding only
73.x: Andhra Pradesh's noted export strengths include Guntur chillies, turmeric, mango pulp, pharmaceuticals from Vizag/Parawada and petroleum products from the Visakhapatnam refinery.
73.tq: Select the option containing the complete cluster of State-specific export items.
73.sec: AP exports - items, ports, share

73.s: Andhra Pradesh ranked what among large States in the NITI Aayog Export Preparedness Index 2024?
73.x: Andhra Pradesh ranked fifth among large States in the NITI Aayog Export Preparedness Index 2024, released in January 2026.
73.tq: Separate the State's rank from the year of the index and its release year.
73.sec: AP exports - items, ports, share

73.s: Which of the following correctly matches a trade concept with its meaning?
o: Terms of trade — quantity restriction on imports
Comparative advantage — specialisation based on lower opportunity cost
73.x: Comparative advantage refers to specialisation in a good with lower opportunity cost. Absolute advantage concerns lower absolute cost, dumping concerns export pricing, and a quota is a quantitative import restriction.
73.tq: Use the defining distinction between absolute cost, opportunity cost, pricing and quantity controls.
73.sec: Trade theory terms

73.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Special Economic Zones (SEZs):
1. The SEZ concept was proposed in the EXIM Policy 1997–2002.
2. The SEZ policy was announced in April 2000.
3. The SEZ Act was enacted in 2005.
4. The SEZ Rules were notified in 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All four statements are correct: the concept was proposed in EXIM Policy 1997–2002, the policy was announced in April 2000, the Act was enacted in 2005 and the Rules were notified in 2006.
73.tq: Check the full sequence of policy concept, policy announcement, Act and Rules.
73.sec: Export promotion zones and bodies - EPZs, SEZs, AEZ nodal agency, facilitation centres

73.s: The nodal agency for Agri Export Zones in India is:
73.x: The Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) is the nodal agency for Agri Export Zones.
73.tq: Identify the institution assigned the specific export-promotion function.
73.sec: Export promotion zones and bodies - EPZs, SEZs, AEZ nodal agency, facilitation centres

73.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: EXIM Bank — Established on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981
APEDA — Established on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981
EXIM Bank — Established in May 2021 at Pune
SEZ Authority — Established in 1965 at Kandla
73.x: EXIM Bank commenced operations on 1 January 1982 under the EXIM Bank Act, 1981.
73.tq: Start from the sure institution-date pair and reject swapped agencies and milestones.
73.sec: Export promotion zones and bodies - EPZs, SEZs, AEZ nodal agency, facilitation centres

73.s: The headquarters of EXIM Bank is located at:
73.x: EXIM Bank is headquartered in Mumbai.
73.tq: Test the location of the institution independently from its establishment date.
73.sec: Export promotion zones and bodies - EPZs, SEZs, AEZ nodal agency, facilitation centres

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a function of EXIM Bank mentioned in relation to export finance?
o: Providing lines of credit to foreign governments
73.x: EXIM Bank provides lines of credit, buyer's and seller's credit, project-export finance and SME export windows. Framing and monitoring foreign trade policy is not its function.
73.tq: Find the institution-function mismatch among closely related trade bodies.
73.sec: Export promotion zones and bodies - EPZs, SEZs, AEZ nodal agency, facilitation centres

73.s:
With reference to Foreign Trade Policy (FTP) 2023, consider the following statements:
1. It came into effect from 1 April 2023.
2. It has a fixed end date of 31 March 2028.
3. It is reviewed as needed.
4. It targets exports of 2 trillion US dollars by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: FTP 2023 came into effect on 1 April 2023, has no fixed end date, is reviewed as needed and targets 2 trillion US dollars in exports by 2030. Statement 2 is false.
73.tq: Spot the false fixed-end-date statement in a policy described as dynamic.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: Which department frames and monitors India's Foreign Trade Policy?
73.x: The Department of Commerce frames and monitors India's Foreign Trade Policy.
73.tq: Apply the ‘who would do this job?’ method to distinguish neighbouring government departments.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: Which of the following is NOT a stated pillar of FTP 2023?
73.x: The stated pillars include duty-free input schemes, Districts as Export Hubs, logistics and better utilisation of FTAs. Compulsory nationalisation of export firms is not a pillar.
73.tq: Identify the invented policy instrument among genuine FTP pillars.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: RoDTEP stands for:
o: Reduction of Duties on Trade and Export Programmes
Rebate of Duties for External Trade and Production
Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products
Refund of Domestic Export Trade Expenses and Production
73.x: RoDTEP means Remission of Duties and Taxes on Export Products.
73.tq: Discriminate between similar-looking expansions of an official acronym.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: RoDTEP replaced which WTO-challenged scheme of FTP 2015–20?
73.x: RoDTEP replaced the WTO-challenged Merchandise Exports from India Scheme (MEIS) of FTP 2015–20.
73.tq: Match the successor scheme with the scheme it replaced.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: The RBI's rupee trade settlement framework operates through:
73.x: The framework operates through Special Rupee Vostro Accounts and is intended to encourage use of the Indian rupee in cross-border trade.
73.tq: Distinguish the specific banking mechanism from other international monetary arrangements.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s: The principal purpose of India's rupee trade settlement framework is to:
o: Replace the WTO dispute settlement system
Encourage the use of the Indian rupee in cross-border trade
73.x: The framework is intended to encourage the use of the Indian rupee in cross-border trade; it does not prohibit all foreign-currency transactions.
73.tq: Apply the stated purpose of a financial mechanism to a practical trade situation.
73.sec: Foreign Trade Policy - latest FTP, RoDTEP, Districts as Export Hubs, rupee settlement

73.s:
Consider the following statements about India's trade agreements:
1. India-UAE CEPA was concluded in 2022.
2. India-Australia ECTA was concluded in 2022.
3. India-EFTA TEPA was signed in March 2024.
4. The India-EFTA TEPA covers Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
73.x: All four statements are correct. The India-EFTA TEPA was signed in March 2024 with Switzerland, Norway, Iceland and Liechtenstein.
73.tq: Verify dates and membership together in a multi-statement agreement question.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
73.x: The India-UAE CEPA was concluded in 2022. The India-Australia ECTA was also concluded in 2022, while the India-EFTA TEPA was signed in March 2024.
73.tq: Use exact agreement-year matching and reject swapped dates.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: The membership of SAFTA comprises:
o: The members of the European Free Trade Association
73.x: SAFTA, the successor to SAPTA, comprises the eight SAARC countries: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, Maldives and Afghanistan.
73.tq: Identify the regional grouping from its institutional predecessor and membership size.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: Which one of the following is NOT a member of SAFTA?
73.x: SAFTA includes the eight SAARC countries, including Bhutan, Afghanistan and Maldives. Myanmar is not among the listed SAFTA members.
73.tq: Find the outsider in a regional-membership list.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: NAMA-11 is a WTO coalition concerned primarily with:
73.x: NAMA-11 is a coalition of developing countries in the WTO dealing with non-agricultural market access; India, Brazil and South Africa are among its members.
73.tq: Expand the acronym conceptually and distinguish the negotiating subject.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: Which of the following countries is specifically mentioned as a member of NAMA-11?
73.x: India is specifically mentioned as a member of the NAMA-11 coalition, along with countries such as Brazil and South Africa.
73.tq: Use the membership clue to distinguish a developing-country WTO coalition from other groups.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: According to the stated trade-agreement count for June 2026, India had:
o: 14 FTAs covering 6 countries and talks with 27 more
42 FTAs covering 15 countries and talks with 27 more
27 FTAs covering 15 countries and talks with 42 more
15 FTAs covering 27 countries and talks with 42 more
73.x: The June 2026 count states that India had 15 FTAs covering 27 countries and was in talks with 42 more countries.
73.tq: Read the three-part numerical relationship carefully: agreements, countries covered and countries under negotiation.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: Which statement best reflects the utilisation of India's FTAs as stated?
o: FTAs cover less than 20% of exports, with utilisation above 75%.
FTAs could cover about 75% of exports, but utilisation is only 20–30%.
FTAs cover about 20–30% of exports, with complete utilisation.
FTAs cover 100% of exports, with utilisation of 50–60%.
73.x: India's FTAs could cover approximately 75% of exports, but their actual utilisation is only around 20–30%.
73.tq: Keep potential coverage and actual utilisation as separate quantities.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: In the third quarter of FY26, India's exports to FTA partners and imports from them respectively:
73.x: Exports to FTA partners fell by 7% year-on-year in Q3 FY26, while imports rose by 6%.
73.tq: Preserve the direction and magnitude of each side of the trade comparison.
73.sec: Trade agreements and WTO - FTAs/CEPAs, SAFTA, NAMA-11, Ministerial Conferences

73.s: After a currency depreciation, the J-curve effect implies that the trade balance generally:
o: Worsens only when exports become cheaper abroad
Remains unchanged because prices do not change
Improves immediately and then worsens permanently
First worsens and improves only after export and import volumes adjust
73.x: Under the J-curve effect, import bills rise immediately after depreciation, so the trade balance initially worsens; it improves later as quantities adjust.
73.tq: Apply the time sequence—initial price effect followed by volume adjustment—to the trade balance.
73.sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

73.s: Which of the following correctly describes the immediate effects of devaluation or depreciation?
o: Exports become cheaper abroad and imports become dearer at home
Exports become dearer abroad and imports become cheaper at home
Both exports and imports become cheaper at home
Neither export nor import prices are affected
73.x: Devaluation or depreciation makes domestic exports cheaper for foreign buyers and imports more expensive in the domestic market.
73.tq: Track the direction of price changes separately in foreign and domestic markets.
73.sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

73.s: According to the Marshall–Lerner condition, devaluation improves the trade balance when:
o: Only export demand is perfectly inelastic
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is greater than one
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is equal to zero
The sum of export and import demand price elasticities is less than one
73.x: The Marshall–Lerner condition is satisfied when the sum of the absolute values of export and import demand price elasticities exceeds one.
73.tq: Recall the threshold condition and distinguish greater than one from less than one.
73.sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

73.s:
Assertion (A): A depreciation may initially worsen a country's trade balance.
Reason (R): Import bills can rise immediately before export and import quantities adjust.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
73.x: Both the assertion and reason are true, and the immediate rise in import bills explains the initial worsening described by the J-curve effect.
73.tq: Test whether the reason explains the time-order mechanism in the assertion.
73.sec: Exchange rate and trade - devaluation, J-curve, Marshall-Lerner

73.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the recent tariff-related trade developments stated for India?
o: US tariffs increased India's exports to the US by 20.4% in September 2025 and eliminated the October deficit.
US tariffs affected only India's services exports and not merchandise trade.
India's exports to the US fell by 7% in October 2025 and the deficit was $2.18 billion.
US tariffs reduced India's exports to the US by 20.4% in September 2025 and the October 2025 deficit reached $21.8 billion.
73.x: The stated figures are a 20.4% fall in exports to the US in September 2025 and an October 2025 trade deficit of $21.8 billion.
73.tq: Match the correct percentage, month and deficit figure without shifting units or periods.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: In August 2026, India's goods exports reportedly:
o: Increased by 6.1%, leaving the deficit unchanged
Declined by 26.1%, widening the trade deficit
Increased by 26.1%, narrowing the trade deficit
Declined by 20.4%, narrowing the trade deficit
73.x: Goods exports rose by 26.1% in August 2026, which narrowed India's trade deficit.
73.tq: Link the percentage change with its stated effect on the trade deficit.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: India was ranked third among Global South countries for:
73.x: India ranked third in the Global South for trade-partner diversity according to the stated UNCTAD assessment.
73.tq: Identify the exact indicator associated with the international ranking.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: Which of the following is NOT listed as a response to India's dependence on China for APIs, solar cells and chips?
73.x: The listed responses are QCOs, NTBs and PLI. Abolition of all import regulations is not listed as a response.
73.tq: Find the policy measure that contradicts the stated strategic response.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: The statement that services may show a surplus while merchandise trade remains structurally in deficit is associated with India's:
o: Absolute advantage in all manufactured goods
73.x: The comparison is explained through India's Ricardian comparative advantage in services, alongside a structural merchandise trade deficit.
73.tq: Connect the observed trade pattern with the specified comparative-advantage explanation.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: Which one of the following statements correctly captures the debate regarding India's FTAs?
o: FTAs have achieved complete utilisation by Indian exporters.
FTAs are criticised only because they prohibit services exports.
FTAs have been criticised for widening deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea and for weak utilisation.
FTAs have eliminated India's merchandise deficit with all Asian partners.
73.x: The stated criticism is that FTAs have widened deficits with ASEAN, Japan and Korea and have suffered from weak utilisation.
73.tq: Select the balanced statement containing both the trade-deficit and utilisation concerns.
73.sec: Universal angles

73.s: Which country is identified as India's largest trade partner in the current assessment mentioned?
73.x: The current assessment identifies China as India's largest trade partner.
73.tq: Distinguish the current partner reference from individual FTA partners.
73.sec: Universal angles

74.s:
Consider the following statements regarding agricultural export promotion:
1. APEDA works under the Department of Commerce.
2. The Agriculture Export Policy, 2018 aimed to double agricultural exports.
3. MPEDA handles marine products.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All three statements are correct. APEDA functions under the Department of Commerce, the Agriculture Export Policy 2018 sought to double agricultural exports, and MPEDA handles marine products.
74.tq: Combine institutional responsibility with policy objectives and sector-specific roles.
74.sec: Agri-export promotion - nodal agency and facilities

74.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Import substitution — Outward-looking strategy for promoting manufactured exports
Import quota — Quantitative restriction on imports
74.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy that seeks to produce import substitutes domestically and reduce import dependence. Export promotion is the outward-looking strategy associated with manufactured exports.
74.tq: Find the reversed meaning in a comparison table.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s: Which of the following best describes import substitution?
o: Increasing dependence on imported capital goods
Promoting only agricultural exports through export subsidies
Reducing import dependence by producing import substitutes at home
74.x: Import substitution is an inward-looking strategy aimed at producing goods domestically in order to reduce import dependency.
74.tq: Apply the inward-looking versus outward-looking distinction to a policy description.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s: The import-substitution strategy in India continued for approximately:
74.x: Import substitution remained the dominant approach in India for about four decades.
74.tq: Test the approximate duration rather than a precise year.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s:
With reference to the 1992 trade-policy changes, consider the following statements:
1. Sixty per cent of foreign exchange was permitted at the market rate.
2. Forty per cent of foreign exchange was permitted at the official rate.
3. Raw materials and capital goods were brought under Open General Licence.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: The 1992 measures provided partial current-account convertibility, with 60% of foreign exchange at the market rate and 40% at the official rate; raw materials and capital goods were also placed under OGL.
74.tq: Check the numerical split together with the associated policy measure.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s:
Arrange the following developments in chronological order:
A. Introduction of Foreign Trade Policy
B. Introduction of EXIM Policy
C. Partial current-account convertibility
D. 1991 Trade Policy shift to a price-based regime
74.x: EXIM Policy began in 1985-88, the 1991 Trade Policy brought the shift to a price-based regime, partial current-account convertibility followed in 1992, and Foreign Trade Policy replaced EXIM Policy from 2004.
74.tq: Anchor the sequence with the earliest EXIM Policy and the latest 2004 Foreign Trade Policy.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s: The EXIM policies introduced during 1985-88 gave way to the Foreign Trade Policy from:
74.x: The earlier EXIM policies gave way to the Foreign Trade Policy framework from 2004.
74.tq: Distinguish the policy transition year from the reform years of 1991 and 1992.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s: The Foreign Trade Policy is administered through the Directorate General of Foreign Trade under the:
o: Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises
74.x: The Foreign Trade Policy is administered by the Department of Commerce, Ministry of Commerce and Industry, through the DGFT.
74.tq: Use the ‘which ministry’ trap to separate the Department of Commerce from neighbouring ministries.
74.sec: Trade policy instruments and history

74.s:
Consider the following statements about the Foreign Trade Policy 2023:
1. It came into force on 1 April 2023.
2. It has a fixed statutory end date.
3. It aims at exports of 2 trillion US dollars by 2030.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: The policy came into force on 1 April 2023 and set an export target of 2 trillion US dollars by 2030. It has no end date, so statement 2 is false.
74.tq: Spot the false fixed-end-date assertion against a policy described as having no end date.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s: Which one of the following is a feature of the Foreign Trade Policy 2023?
o: A shift from remission and entitlement support to only quantitative restrictions
A shift from incentives towards remission and entitlement-based support
A complete withdrawal of electronic initiatives
74.x: FTP 2023 shifts the emphasis from conventional incentives towards remission and entitlement-based support, while also promoting e-initiatives and merchanting trade.
74.tq: Reject the options that reverse the direction of policy change.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s: The initiative ‘Districts as Export Hubs’ under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023 seeks to:
o: Promote export potential at the district level
Concentrate all exports in metropolitan ports
74.x: Districts as Export Hubs is intended to identify and promote export potential across districts.
74.tq: Infer the decentralised policy objective from the name and institutional context.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s:
Which of the following combinations is associated with the Foreign Trade Policy 2023?
1. Rupee trade settlement
2. New Towns of Export Excellence
3. One-time amnesty for certain export-obligation defaults
4. Promotion of merchanting trade
74.x: FTP 2023 includes rupee trade settlement, new Towns of Export Excellence, a one-time amnesty for EPCG and Advance Authorisation export-obligation defaults, and promotion of merchanting trade.
74.tq: Recognise the cluster of distinctive policy features rather than an isolated incentive.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s:
Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2023, the green-technology list under EPCG was widened to include which of the following?
1. Battery electric vehicles
2. Vertical farming
3. Wastewater recycling
4. Rainwater harvesting
5. Green hydrogen
74.x: The widened EPCG green-technology list includes battery electric vehicles, vertical farming, wastewater recycling, rainwater harvesting and green hydrogen.
74.tq: Test completeness of a named list by checking every listed item.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s: Under the Foreign Trade Policy 2015-20, MEIS and SEIS respectively related to:
74.x: MEIS provided support for exports of goods, while SEIS related to exports of services under FTP 2015-20.
74.tq: Separate the two similar-sounding schemes by their covered sectors.
74.sec: Foreign Trade Policy 2023 - features

74.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched?
o: DGFT — Headquarters at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi
EXIM Bank — Headquarters at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi
ECGC — Issues Foreign Trade Policy authorisations
EPCs — Provides buyers’ and sellers’ credit
74.x: DGFT is headquartered at Vanijya Bhavan, New Delhi. DGFT issues FTP authorisations; EXIM Bank provides lines of credit and buyers’ and sellers’ credit, while ECGC provides export credit insurance.
74.tq: Match each body with its institutional role and location.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s:
The Directorate General of Foreign Trade performs which of the following functions?
1. Issuing Foreign Trade Policy authorisations
2. Running Districts as Export Hubs
3. Running Export Promotion Mission
4. Providing export credit insurance
74.x: DGFT issues FTP authorisations and runs Districts as Export Hubs and the Export Promotion Mission. Export credit insurance is provided by ECGC, so statement 4 is false.
74.tq: Separate the functions of DGFT from the insurance role of ECGC.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: EPCs and Commodity Boards primarily perform which function in export promotion?
o: They insure all export credit against political risks.
They issue import licences for all commodities.
They determine the exchange rate for export transactions.
They promote sectoral exports and channel Market Access Initiative support.
74.x: Export Promotion Councils and Commodity Boards promote exports in particular sectors and channel Market Access Initiative support.
74.tq: Identify the sectoral promotional role rather than a financial or regulatory function.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: Which of the following is NOT a function or activity associated with EXIM Bank?
o: Issuing export credit insurance as its principal role
74.x: EXIM Bank provides lines of credit, buyer’s credit, seller’s credit and support for project exports. Export credit insurance is principally associated with ECGC.
74.tq: Find the financial function assigned to the neighbouring institution ECGC.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: The principal role of ECGC is to provide:
o: Foreign exchange at the official rate
74.x: ECGC provides export credit insurance and implements the RELIEF 2026 scheme.
74.tq: Distinguish an insurance institution from export-financing and regulatory bodies.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: NIRVIK, introduced in 2019, was associated with:
o: Duty-free import of all consumer goods
Export promotion through Districts as Export Hubs
Larger ECGC insurance cover for export credit
74.x: NIRVIK was introduced in 2019 to provide larger ECGC insurance cover for export credit.
74.tq: Match the scheme with the institution whose coverage it strengthened.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: Export Houses are classified as One-Star to Five-Star Status Holders primarily on the basis of their:
74.x: Status-holder classification from One-Star to Five-Star is based on export performance.
74.tq: Identify the qualifying criterion rather than an unrelated trade statistic.
74.sec: Trade promotion and export credit bodies

74.s: RoDTEP replaced which scheme and seeks to refund which category of burden?
o: SEIS; only income tax paid by exporters
MEIS; unrebated central, state and local taxes
RoSL; only customs duties on imported inputs
74.x: RoDTEP replaced MEIS and refunds unrebated central, state and local taxes, including electricity duty and VAT on transport fuel.
74.tq: Separate the replaced scheme from the similar RoSCTL and RoSL schemes.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: RoDTEP is implemented online by the:
74.x: RoDTEP is run online by the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
74.tq: Use the implementing-body trap among institutions active in foreign trade.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: RoSCTL replaced RoSL and provides a rebate mainly for:
74.x: RoSCTL replaced RoSL and provides a rebate for apparel and made-ups.
74.tq: Match the scheme with its specific product category.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Advance Authorisation — Duty-free import of inputs for export production
SEIS — Reward for services exports under FTP 2015-20
EPCG — Zero-duty import of capital goods against export obligation
Duty drawback — Refund of income tax on export profits
74.x: Duty drawback refunds customs duty on imported inputs used in exports; it does not refund income tax on export profits.
74.tq: Reject the option that changes a customs-duty refund into an income-tax refund.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. SEIS was a services-export reward under FTP 2015-20.
2. SEIS has been discontinued.
3. EPCG permits zero-duty import of capital goods against an export obligation.
4. Advance Authorisation permits duty-free import of inputs for export production.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All four statements are correct. SEIS was a services-export reward under FTP 2015-20 and is discontinued; EPCG and Advance Authorisation provide the stated import-related facilities.
74.tq: Check each scheme against its objective and current status.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: The Export Promotion Mission has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for which period?
74.x: The Export Promotion Mission has an outlay of ₹25,060 crore for FY 2025-26 to FY 2030-31.
74.tq: Match the outlay with the correct implementation period.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: Which of the following statements regarding the Export Promotion Mission is correct?
o: It is run by ECGC and targets only large exporters.
It is run by DGFT, merges Interest Equalisation and Market Access Initiative, and targets MSMEs and first-time exporters.
It is run by CBIC and concerns only customs assessment.
It is run by EXIM Bank and replaces the Foreign Trade Policy.
74.x: The Export Promotion Mission is run by DGFT, merges the Interest Equalisation and Market Access Initiative, and focuses on MSMEs and first-time exporters.
74.tq: Identify the implementing body, merger and target beneficiaries together.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: Which of the following is NOT included among the Niryat Disha tools?
74.x: The Niryat Disha tools are TRACE, FLOW, LIFT and INSIGHT. NIRVIK is a separate scheme associated with enhanced ECGC insurance cover.
74.tq: Separate a similarly themed export scheme from the members of a named tool list.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: The RELIEF Scheme 2026, implemented through ECGC, provides support mainly for:
o: Interest subsidy on domestic housing loans
War-risk and logistics costs in West Asia
74.x: RELIEF Scheme 2026 provides support for war-risk and logistics costs in West Asia through ECGC under the Export Promotion Mission.
74.tq: Link the risk described in the scenario with the specialised insurance-support scheme.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s:
Which of the following statements about RELIEF Scheme 2026 is correct?
1. It has an allocation of ₹497 crore under the Export Promotion Mission.
2. Egypt and Jordan were added in April 2026.
3. It is implemented through ECGC.
74.x: RELIEF Scheme 2026 has an allocation of ₹497 crore under the Export Promotion Mission, is implemented through ECGC, and included Egypt and Jordan from April 2026.
74.tq: Combine the scheme’s amount, implementing agency and geographical expansion.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: For leather and textile garments and footwear, the export period under Advance Authorisation was extended in Budget 2026-27 from:
74.x: Budget 2026-27 extended the Advance Authorisation export period for the specified products from six months to one year.
74.tq: Compare the original and revised durations directly.
74.sec: Export incentive schemes - replaced scheme and objective

74.s: Which document is an importer’s order to buy goods?
74.x: An indent is the importer’s order placed to buy goods.
74.tq: Match the document with the stage of the import transaction at which it is used.
74.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

74.s: A shipping bill is primarily used as:
o: A document conferring title to imported goods
An importer’s order for purchasing goods
A customs document for clearing export goods
A ship’s acknowledgement of goods loaded on board
74.x: A shipping bill is the customs document used for clearing goods for export.
74.tq: Distinguish the customs-clearance document from shipping-company documents.
74.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

74.s: Which document acknowledges that goods have been loaded on board by the ship’s mate?
74.x: A mate’s receipt is the acknowledgement by the ship’s mate that goods have been loaded on board.
74.tq: Use the document’s issuing person to identify its purpose.
74.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

74.s: A bill of lading serves as:
o: A shipping company’s receipt and a document of title to the goods
An exporter’s application for a duty drawback
A customs order fixing the tariff rate
74.x: A bill of lading is the shipping company’s receipt and also functions as a document of title to the goods.
74.tq: Select the option that contains both parts of the document’s legal function.
74.sec: Export-import procedure - purpose of documents, rules of origin

74.s: The SEZ Act was enacted in which year?
74.x: The SEZ Act was enacted in 2005.
74.tq: Discriminate between closely spaced policy years.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s:
With reference to Special Economic Zones, consider the following statements:
1. They are treated as foreign territory for trade and tariff purposes.
2. They are designated duty-free enclaves.
3. One hundred per cent FDI is permitted through the automatic route for most manufacturing activities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All three statements are correct. SEZs are duty-free enclaves treated as foreign territory for trade and tariffs, and 100% FDI is allowed through the automatic route for most manufacturing activities.
74.tq: Check each statement against the defining features and benefit provisions of SEZs.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: SEZ — units that must be located anywhere outside a designated enclave
74.x: EHTP units receive duty-free inputs relating to electronics hardware. EOUs deal with goods generally, while STPs deal with software.
74.tq: Start from the sure sector-to-incentive pair and eliminate swapped associations.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s:
Consider the following statements regarding EOUs, EHTPs and STPs:
1. These units export all their output.
2. They can be located anywhere.
3. They receive duty-free inputs appropriate to their activity.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: EOUs, EHTPs and STPs export all their output, may be located anywhere, and receive duty-free inputs suited to their respective activities.
74.tq: Test the distinction between location-based SEZs and activity-based export units.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s:
Which one of the following correctly identifies the input category associated with each export-oriented unit?
1. EOU — goods
2. EHTP — electronics hardware
3. STP — software
74.x: EOUs receive duty-free goods inputs, EHTPs receive electronics hardware inputs, and STPs receive software-related inputs.
74.tq: Match each abbreviation with its specialised activity before selecting the combination.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s: The Budget 2026–27 proposed measures concerning SEZs primarily in order to address which issue?
o: Idle manufacturing capacity affected by global trade
Absence of automatic FDI in manufacturing
Shortage of agricultural land in export districts
74.x: The Budget 2026–27 measures were aimed at using idle SEZ manufacturing capacity affected by global trade conditions.
74.tq: Link the policy measure to the specific problem it seeks to address.
74.sec: EOUs, EHTP, STP and SEZ - distinction and benefits

74.s: The Districts as Export Hubs initiative was launched in which year?
74.x: The Districts as Export Hubs initiative was launched in 2019 under the Foreign Trade Policy framework.
74.tq: Use the launch-year clue and distinguish it from later implementation measures.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: Which authority functions as the nodal agency for the Districts as Export Hubs initiative?
74.x: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade (DGFT) is the nodal agency for the Districts as Export Hubs initiative.
74.tq: Apply the who-would-do-this-job method to export-trade administration.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s:
With reference to the Districts as Export Hubs initiative, consider the following statements:
1. State and District Export Promotion Committees are associated with the initiative.
2. District Export Action Plans are prepared under the initiative.
3. The initiative was launched in 2019 under the Foreign Trade Policy.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: All three statements are correct. The initiative involves State and District Export Promotion Committees, District Export Action Plans, and was launched in 2019 under the Foreign Trade Policy.
74.tq: Combine institutional, planning and chronological clues in a coded-statement question.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: District Export Action Plans under the Districts as Export Hubs initiative relate to how many districts?
74.x: District Export Action Plans were provided for 590 districts. Of these, 249 districts were notified.
74.tq: Separate the total coverage figure from the notified-district figure.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: How many districts had been notified under the Districts as Export Hubs initiative as indicated in the available formulation?
74.x: The number of notified districts was 249, while District Export Action Plans covered 590 districts.
74.tq: Watch for the number-pair trap involving total plans and notified districts.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: In the phased rollout of September 2026, which of the following developments was associated with the Districts as Export Hubs initiative?
o: LEADS was merged into SWIFT for district-level imports
District Export Action Plans were replaced by state-level tariff plans
ODOP was merged into DEH and Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras were introduced for postal exports
SEZs were merged into EOUs and customs clearance was withdrawn
74.x: The September 2026 phased rollout merged One District One Product (ODOP) into Districts as Export Hubs and provided Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras for postal exports.
74.tq: Identify the paired developments belonging to the same rollout.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: Which one of the following is intended to facilitate postal exports under the September 2026 phased rollout of the Districts as Export Hubs initiative?
74.x: Dak Ghar Niryat Kendras were associated with facilitating postal exports.
74.tq: Use the distinctive institutional name to identify the relevant function.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s:
Which of the following pairs of Andhra Pradesh export products and districts is correctly matched?
1. Guntur chillies — Guntur
2. Shrimp — West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore
3. Mango pulp — Andhra Pradesh
74.x: Guntur chillies are associated with Guntur, shrimp with West Godavari, Krishna and Nellore, and mango pulp is an identified Andhra Pradesh export product.
74.tq: Match the product with its stated district or regional association.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: Vizag is identified in the context of Andhra Pradesh exports particularly for which product?
74.x: Vizag is identified with pharmaceutical exports. Turmeric, mango pulp and tobacco are separate export-related products or concerns in the material.
74.tq: Discriminate among nearby Andhra Pradesh export products and locations.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with an Andhra Pradesh export product association?
74.x: Krishna is associated with shrimp along with West Godavari and Nellore; it is not identified as a turmeric-only export association.
74.tq: Find the option that distorts a correct product-location association by adding an unsupported exclusive claim.
74.sec: Districts as Export Hubs - AP

74.s: ICEGATE is best described as which of the following?
o: A postal export network of India Post
A logistics ranking index of NITI Aayog
A single-window system for foreign investment approvals
A customs e-filing portal of CBIC
74.x: ICEGATE is the customs e-filing portal of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC).
74.tq: Identify the responsible authority behind the digital trade platform.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s: The SWIFT system in the context of trade facilitation is associated with which function?
74.x: SWIFT functions as a single window for import clearance.
74.tq: Separate a clearance mechanism from portals, rankings and export-support institutions.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. ICEGATE — Customs e-filing portal
2. SWIFT — Single window for import clearance
3. LEADS — Ranking States on logistics
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
74.x: All three pairs are correctly matched. ICEGATE handles customs e-filing, SWIFT supports single-window import clearance, and LEADS ranks States on logistics.
74.tq: Start from the familiar platform-function pairs and check all three associations.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s:
Which of the following pairs of initiatives and launch years is correctly matched?
1. PM Gati Shakti — 2021
2. National Logistics Policy — 2022
74.x: PM Gati Shakti was launched in 2021 and the National Logistics Policy was launched in 2022.
74.tq: Fix the two dates first and verify the pair rather than inferring from policy names.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s: What is the principal common objective of PM Gati Shakti and the National Logistics Policy in relation to foreign trade?
o: To increase import duties on manufactured goods
To restrict the movement of cargo through ports
74.x: PM Gati Shakti and the National Logistics Policy aim to reduce export logistics costs and improve trade facilitation.
74.tq: Identify the shared policy objective rather than confusing it with tariff or regulatory measures.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s: The LEADS index is associated with ranking States on which aspect?
74.x: The LEADS index ranks States on logistics performance.
74.tq: Use the expansion and function of the index to reject unrelated economic indicators.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes the Export Preparedness Index from the LEADS index?
o: The Export Preparedness Index ranks customs portals, whereas LEADS ranks SEZs.
The Export Preparedness Index measures postal exports, whereas LEADS measures FDI.
The Export Preparedness Index ranks States on export preparedness, whereas LEADS ranks States on logistics.
Both indices exclusively rank districts on agricultural exports.
74.x: The Export Preparedness Index assesses export preparedness, while LEADS is concerned with logistics performance. Andhra Pradesh's stated position in the former was fifth among large States in 2024.
74.tq: Split the options by comparing the subject and unit of measurement of each index.
74.sec: Trade facilitation and logistics - AP rank

74.s: Which recent development was identified as having disrupted cargo movement and prompted procedural flexibility in export authorisations?
o: The merger of ODOP with DEH
A global shortage of software exports
The introduction of the LEADS index
74.x: The West Asia conflict disrupted cargo movement, following which the Government allowed procedural flexibility in export authorisations.
74.tq: Connect the external event with its direct trade-policy consequence.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: In response to cargo disruption caused by the West Asia conflict, the Government allowed flexibility primarily in relation to which of the following?
74.x: The Government allowed procedural flexibility in export authorisations in response to cargo disruption caused by the West Asia conflict.
74.tq: Match the emergency response with the administrative instrument affected.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s:
Which of the following were among the export-related matters raised by Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu?
1. Regulation of fish-meal exports
2. Export incentives for aquaculture
3. Export incentives for tobacco
Which of the statements given above are correct?
74.x: The matters raised included regulation of fish-meal exports and export incentives for both aquaculture and tobacco.
74.tq: Check whether all three sector-specific demands belong to the same policy intervention.
74.sec: Universal angles

74.s: The Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister sought export incentives for which combination of sectors?
74.x: Export incentives were sought for aquaculture and tobacco, along with a request to regulate fish-meal exports.
74.tq: Discriminate between product examples and the sectors specifically linked to the demand for incentives.
74.sec: Universal angles

75.s: Under the Balance of Payments framework, which of the following best distinguishes the presentation followed by the IMF from that generally followed by the Reserve Bank of India?
o: The IMF uses only current and capital accounts, whereas the RBI uses current, capital and financial accounts separately.
The IMF uses only trade and services accounts, whereas the RBI uses current and financial accounts.
The IMF uses current, capital and financial accounts, whereas the RBI generally combines the capital and financial accounts.
Both the IMF and the RBI invariably present the Balance of Payments through exactly three separate accounts.
75.x: Under BPM6, the IMF distinguishes current, capital and financial accounts. The RBI generally combines the capital and financial accounts under the heading ‘capital account’.
75.tq: Separate the IMF classification from the RBI presentation instead of treating the terms as identical.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the account in which it is recorded?
o: Foreign Currency Assets — Current account under merchandise trade
75.x: Remittances are recorded in the current account, under invisibles and specifically private transfers. Software exports are services, while NRI deposits and foreign currency assets belong to capital or reserve-related transactions.
75.tq: Identify the account by separating visible trade, invisibles and financial flows.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Balance of Payments:
1. The current account includes merchandise trade and transactions in services.
2. Primary income includes interest, dividends and profits.
3. Secondary income includes remittances, gifts and grants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: All three statements are correct. The current account covers visible trade, services, primary income and secondary income.
75.tq: Group the components of the current account before evaluating the coded combinations.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: A capital-account transaction involving the purchase of foreign assets by residents is recorded as:
o: A current-account credit because assets are goods
A debit because foreign exchange flows out for acquiring the assets
A credit because foreign exchange enters the country
75.x: Purchase of foreign assets by residents is a capital-account debit. Conversely, sale of Indian assets to foreigners is recorded as a credit.
75.tq: Follow the direction of the financial flow to distinguish a debit from a credit.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which of the following combinations consists exclusively of capital and financial account items?
o: Travel receipts, transport services and private transfers
FDI, FPI, ADRs and external commercial borrowings
Merchandise exports, software services and remittances
75.x: FDI, FPI, ADRs and external commercial borrowings are capital or financial account transactions. The other combinations contain current-account items.
75.tq: Eliminate current-account items such as goods, services, income and transfers.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which one of the following is NOT generally included among the invisible components of the current account?
75.x: Merchandise imports are visible trade and form part of the trade balance. Software, travel, banking and insurance are invisible services.
75.tq: Find the visible-trade item among services and other invisible transactions.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: The balance of the current account is represented by which of the following expressions?
o: Exports minus imports of goods and services plus net primary and net secondary income
Capital inflows minus capital outflows plus errors and omissions
Exports and imports of goods only plus changes in foreign exchange reserves
Foreign direct investment plus portfolio investment minus external debt
75.x: The current-account balance equals exports minus imports of goods and services, plus net primary income and net secondary income.
75.tq: Reconstruct the identity by adding goods, services, primary income and secondary income.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which of the following correctly states the financing relationship associated with a current account deficit?
o: A current account deficit automatically creates a capital-account deficit of the same amount.
A current account deficit has no relationship with capital and financial flows.
A current account deficit can be financed only by reducing merchandise imports.
A current account deficit must be financed by a capital-account surplus, subject to errors and omissions and reserve changes.
75.x: A current account deficit generally requires financing through capital and financial inflows, including a capital-account surplus or reserve drawdown, within the overall Balance of Payments identity.
75.tq: Use the BoP identity to connect a deficit in one account with financing flows in another.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which of the following correctly represents the Balance of Payments identity?
o: Current balance + capital balance + financial balance + errors and omissions = zero
Current balance + merchandise exports = financial balance
Current balance − capital balance = trade balance
75.x: The Balance of Payments identity is current balance plus capital balance plus financial balance plus errors and omissions equal to zero.
75.tq: Recall the complete identity rather than restricting the BoP to the trade balance.
75.sec: BoP structure - current account vs capital account items

75.s: Which one of the following is the correct descending order of the major components of India’s foreign exchange reserves by relative size?
o: FCA, gold, SDRs and reserve tranche positions
SDRs, FCA, gold, reserve tranche positions
Reserve tranche position, SDRs, gold, FCA
75.x: Foreign Currency Assets are the largest component, followed by gold. SDRs and the reserve tranche position are comparatively small.
75.tq: Rank the reserve components by relative size before examining the alternatives.
75.sec: Forex reserves - components, shares, reserve tranche, import cover, rank

75.s: The Reserve Tranche Position of a country in the International Monetary Fund refers to:
o: The share of SDRs allocated to private commercial banks
The total amount of gold held by the country
The portion of the IMF quota that can be drawn without conditions
The country’s annual export earnings deposited with the IMF
75.x: The reserve tranche is the part of a member country’s IMF quota that it can draw without conditionality.
75.tq: Use the precise meaning of ‘tranche’ instead of confusing it with SDR allocation or gold holdings.
75.sec: Forex reserves - components, shares, reserve tranche, import cover, rank

75.s: In the context of foreign exchange reserves, ‘import cover’ refers to:
o: The share of imports paid for through barter
The proportion of imports financed through domestic taxation
The number of months for which existing reserves can finance imports
The percentage of imports subject to customs duty
75.x: Import cover measures how long a country’s foreign exchange reserves can finance its imports. India’s reserves were reported to provide cover of over 11 months in the stated period.
75.tq: Interpret import cover as a time measure, not a tariff or financing percentage.
75.sec: Forex reserves - components, shares, reserve tranche, import cover, rank

75.s: India’s foreign exchange reserves of approximately $701.4 billion were reported to provide import cover of about:
75.x: Reserves of approximately $701.4 billion were associated with import cover of about 11 months.
75.tq: Match the reserve figure with its stated duration of import cover.
75.sec: Forex reserves - components, shares, reserve tranche, import cover, rank

75.s: According to the stated reserve position, India’s foreign exchange reserves declined by approximately how much in FY 2026 while defending the rupee?
75.x: The stated decline in foreign exchange reserves during FY 2026, associated with defending the rupee, was approximately $23.6 billion.
75.tq: Read the numerical change as a reserve movement rather than as the total reserve level.
75.sec: Forex reserves - components, shares, reserve tranche, import cover, rank

75.s: Which one of the following sets contains only expenditure-switching measures for correcting a Balance of Payments deficit?
o: Devaluation, import tariffs and export incentives
Reduced government spending, import quotas and higher interest rates
Fiscal restraint, monetary tightening and reduction in public expenditure
Higher interest rates, higher taxes and reduced government spending
75.x: Expenditure-switching measures shift demand from foreign goods towards domestic goods and include devaluation, import restrictions and export incentives. The other alternatives are expenditure-reducing measures.
75.tq: Classify policies according to whether they switch demand or reduce total expenditure.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: Which of the following is an expenditure-reducing measure used to correct a Balance of Payments deficit?
o: Tight monetary policy through higher interest rates
75.x: Tight monetary policy, including higher interest rates, reduces aggregate expenditure and imports. Devaluation, import substitution and export promotion are expenditure-switching measures.
75.tq: Identify the policy that reduces aggregate demand rather than redirecting it.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Devaluation can make domestic goods cheaper relative to foreign goods.
2. Import quotas can switch expenditure towards domestically produced goods.
3. Increasing government spending on domestic projects is a standard expenditure-switching measure.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Increasing government spending is not a standard correction measure here because it can raise demand and imports rather than switch expenditure away from foreign goods.
75.tq: Spot the wrong policy by asking whether it redirects expenditure or increases demand.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: Which of the following is NOT ordinarily regarded as a measure for correcting a Balance of Payments deficit?
o: Increasing government spending on domestic projects
75.x: Increasing government spending on domestic projects can raise demand and imports and is therefore not ordinarily treated as a corrective measure in this context. Devaluation, import duties and attracting FDI can help address external imbalance.
75.tq: Use the demand effect of government spending to eliminate the incorrect correction measure.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s:
Arrange the following measures in the order in which they are associated with expenditure switching rather than expenditure reduction:
A. Devaluation
B. Fiscal restraint
C. Import quotas
D. Higher interest rates
75.x: Devaluation and import quotas are expenditure-switching measures, whereas fiscal restraint and higher interest rates are expenditure-reducing measures. The sequence groups the switching measures first and the reducing measures afterwards.
75.tq: Classify each item before arranging the sequence.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: When a country’s foreign exchange reserves are insufficient to cover its Balance of Payments deficit, which institution may be approached as a lender of last resort in this context?
75.x: The International Monetary Fund may provide assistance when a country cannot cover its external deficit from its reserves and other available sources.
75.tq: Match the external-payments problem with the institution associated with balance-of-payments assistance.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: Which one of the following combinations contains measures classified under ‘other’ or financing measures rather than pure expenditure switching?
o: Foreign loans, IMF assistance and encouraging FDI
Devaluation, import quotas and import substitution
Export promotion, tourist incentives and exchange depreciation
Import duties, export incentives and currency depreciation
75.x: Foreign loans, IMF assistance and encouraging FDI provide financing or external support. The other combinations contain expenditure-switching measures.
75.tq: Separate financing measures from policies that alter relative prices or demand between domestic and foreign goods.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: During the reported Iran-related rise in fuel and fertiliser prices, the appeal to reduce import-linked consumption of items such as gold and fuel represented primarily:
o: An expenditure-reducing approach based exclusively on higher interest rates
A policy to increase merchandise imports
An expenditure-switching approach to reduce import demand
75.x: Reducing consumption of import-linked goods switches expenditure away from imports and can lessen pressure on the Balance of Payments. It is not the same as monetary tightening or capital-account liberalisation.
75.tq: Apply the switching-versus-reducing distinction to a contemporary policy situation.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: The increase in import duty on gold, when used to reduce external pressure, is best classified as:
75.x: A higher import duty makes imported gold less attractive and helps switch demand towards domestic alternatives or away from imports. It is therefore an expenditure-switching measure.
75.tq: Trace how an import duty changes the relative attractiveness of foreign goods.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: Which of the following statements about the reported external position during the Iran conflict is correct?
o: The situation was compared with the fragile external position associated with India’s 2013 ‘Fragile Five’ phase.
The Balance of Payments was described as strong and unrelated to import prices.
The situation led to the abolition of import duties on gold.
The external concern arose solely from a fall in domestic tax revenue.
75.x: The reported weakness in the Balance of Payments was compared with India’s 2013 ‘Fragile Five’ phase, amid pressure from higher fuel and fertiliser prices.
75.tq: Use the distinctive comparison phrase and reject explanations not linked to import-price pressure.
75.sec: BoP disequilibrium correction - switching vs reducing, IMF role

75.s: For how many consecutive years did India record a current account surplus during the period 2001-02 to 2003-04?
75.x: India recorded a current account surplus for three consecutive years from 2001-02 to 2003-04.
75.tq: Match the duration directly with the specified financial-year range.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India’s current account position:
1. The current account recorded a surplus in the fourth quarter of 2023-24.
2. The surplus was driven by a surge in services exports.
3. The surplus was primarily caused by a sharp rise in gold imports.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false because the surplus was associated with a surge in services exports, not a rise in gold imports.
75.tq: Separate the stated cause of a surplus from a plausible but opposite trade-pressure factor.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: In the first quarter of 2026-27, India’s current account deficit was reported at approximately:
o: $4.2 billion, or 0.5 per cent of GDP
$13.2 billion, or 1.3 per cent of GDP
$1.3 billion, or 0.2 per cent of GDP
$25.2 billion, or 0.6 per cent of GDP
75.x: In Q1 2026-27, the CAD was $4.2 billion, equivalent to 0.5 per cent of GDP, compared with 0.4 per cent a year earlier.
75.tq: Distinguish the quarterly figure from the full-year and other quarterly CAD figures.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the major components of India’s current account position in the first quarter of 2026-27?
o: Merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion
Merchandise gap of $51.6 billion, net services of $86.1 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion
Merchandise gap of $25.2 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $13.2 billion
Merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $10.5 billion and net primary income outgo of $51.6 billion
75.x: The Q1 FY27 figures were a merchandise gap of $86.1 billion, net services of $51.6 billion and net primary income outgo of $10.5 billion.
75.tq: Use component-value matching to prevent interchange of closely related external-sector figures.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: The record services surplus of $188.8 billion in FY25 financed approximately what proportion of the merchandise deficit?
75.x: The record services surplus of $188.8 billion in FY25 financed about two-thirds of the merchandise deficit. Remittances also acted as a cushion.
75.tq: Identify the comparative proportion rather than treating the services surplus as full financing of the merchandise deficit.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: The external-sector recovery in FY24 was mainly associated with:
o: A decline in remittances and a rise in primary-income outgo
A complete elimination of the merchandise deficit
Moderation in merchandise exports along with a sharp fall in imports
A sharp rise in merchandise imports and a fall in services exports
75.x: The FY24 external-sector recovery came from moderation in merchandise exports accompanied by a sharp fall in imports.
75.tq: Select the precise cause-effect combination and reject reversed trade trends.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s:
Which of the following are structural causes of India’s current account deficit?
1. Dependence on imported oil and gold
2. Low export competitiveness
3. Savings-investment gap
4. Temporary global slowdown alone
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
75.x: Imported oil and gold, low export competitiveness and the savings-investment gap are structural causes. A temporary global slowdown is a cyclical cause, not a structural cause.
75.tq: Classify permanent structural pressures separately from temporary cyclical shocks.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: Which one of the following combinations correctly describes the RBI’s monthly external-sector data mentioned for June and July 2026?
o: June CAD of $20.8 billion; July capital-account surplus of $6.2 billion and overall BoP surplus of $27.7 billion
June CAD of $27.7 billion; July capital-account surplus of $6.2 billion and overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion
June CAD of $6.2 billion; July capital-account surplus of $27.7 billion and overall BoP surplus of $20.8 billion
June CAD of $6.2 billion; July capital-account deficit of $27.7 billion and overall BoP deficit of $20.8 billion
75.x: The RBI reported a CAD of $6.2 billion in June 2026. In July 2026, the capital account showed a $27.7 billion surplus and the overall BoP showed a $20.8 billion surplus.
75.tq: Keep the month and the three external-account values paired correctly.
75.sec: Current account deficit - trend, surplus years, reasons  [APPSC]

75.s: Special Drawing Rights (SDRs) were created by the International Monetary Fund in:
75.x: The IMF created SDRs in 1969 to supplement the official reserves of its member countries.
75.tq: Recall the institutional origin and year of creation without confusing it with later currency or convertibility milestones.
75.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

75.s:
With reference to Special Drawing Rights, consider the following statements:
1. SDR is an interest-bearing reserve asset.
2. SDRs are exchangeable for freely usable currencies.
3. SDRs are physical gold coins issued by the IMF.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: SDRs are interest-bearing reserve assets exchangeable for freely usable currencies. They are not physical gold coins; they are often described as ‘paper gold’.
75.tq: Reject the literal interpretation of a popular descriptive term such as ‘paper gold’.
75.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

75.s: The form in which Special Drawing Rights are maintained is best described as:
75.x: SDRs exist as book-keeping or accounting entries in the IMF’s records; they are not physical currency or metal.
75.tq: Distinguish the reserve-asset concept from a physical medium of payment.
75.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

75.s: Which one of the following is NOT included in the SDR basket?
75.x: The SDR basket contains the US dollar, euro, Chinese renminbi, Japanese yen and pound sterling. The Indian rupee is not included.
75.tq: Find the outsider in a named five-currency basket.
75.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

75.s: The Chinese renminbi was added to the SDR basket in:
75.x: The Chinese renminbi was added to the IMF’s SDR basket in 2016.
75.tq: Use the exact inclusion year rather than the years associated with other IMF reforms.
75.sec: SDR - nature, form, basket  [APPSC]

75.s: Which one of the following correctly distinguishes FERA from FEMA?
o: FERA was a restrictive criminal law, whereas FEMA is a liberal civil law concerned with management and regulation
FERA followed a liberal approach, whereas FEMA imposed strict control over outflow
FERA was a civil law, whereas FEMA was a criminal law
Both FERA and FEMA were identical in nature and approach
75.x: FERA 1973 was restrictive and criminal in nature, focusing on control of foreign exchange outflow. FEMA 1999 is a civil law based on management and regulation with a more liberal approach.
75.tq: Compare the legal character and policy approach of the two paired statutes.
75.sec: FERA to FEMA  [other exams]

75.s:
Consider the following statements regarding FEMA:
1. Its replacement was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget.
2. FEMA was enacted in 1999.
3. FEMA came into force on 1 June 2000.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
75.x: All three statements are correct: replacement was proposed in the 1997-98 Budget, FEMA was enacted in 1999, and it came into force on 1 June 2000.
75.tq: Track a law through proposal, enactment and commencement instead of treating them as one date.
75.sec: FERA to FEMA  [other exams]

75.s: Which of the following correctly represents the external capital-flow position of India in FY26?
o: FPI outflows of $44.0 billion and net FDI of $16.4 billion
FPI outflows of $16.4 billion and net FDI of $6.9 billion
FPI inflows of $6.9 billion and net FDI of $16.4 billion
FPI inflows of $16.4 billion and net FDI of $44.0 billion
75.x: In FY26, FPIs withdrew $16.4 billion, while net FDI was only $6.9 billion. A separate estimate placed FY26 net FDI at $7.6 billion.
75.tq: Check both the direction of the flow and the value before selecting the option.
75.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

75.s: During 2022-23 to 2025-26, gross equity FDI of $317.8 billion was reduced by which combination of outflows?
o: Repatriation and disinvestment of $44.0 billion and dividends of $127 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $178.9 billion and dividends of $118.9 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $317.8 billion and dividends of $6.9 billion
Repatriation and disinvestment of $118.9 billion and dividends of $178.9 billion
75.x: Gross equity FDI was $317.8 billion, while repatriation and disinvestment amounted to $178.9 billion and dividends to $118.9 billion.
75.tq: Match each outflow category with its exact figure rather than merely adding the two amounts.
75.sec: Capital flight and external vulnerability  [other exams]

75.s: The post-1991 pattern in which capital surplus covered the current account deficit was disrupted because:
o: The IMF abolished SDR allocations after 2024
Services exports became permanently negative after 2024
Capital inflows shrank from the middle of 2024
75.x: Since mid-2024, capital inflows have shrunk, breaking the earlier pattern of capital surplus financing the current account deficit.
75.tq: Identify the stated turning point and avoid substituting unrelated external-sector developments.
