82.tq: Test the year and the specific criticism associated with a similar-sounding benchmark.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: The Base Rate system, introduced on 1 July 2010, was based on
82.x: The Base Rate was the minimum lending rate based on the average cost of funds and was introduced on 1 July 2010.
82.tq: Distinguish the cost-based basis of the Base Rate from external-market benchmarks.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s:
Which of the following components is included in the computation of MCLR?
1. Marginal cost of funds
2. Cost of maintaining CRR and SLR
3. Operating cost
4. Tenor premium
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: MCLR incorporates marginal cost of funds, the cost of CRR/SLR, operating cost and a tenor premium.
82.tq: Recognise a complete list question by checking whether each component belongs to the stated formula.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s:
The MCLR framework was intended to achieve which of the following?
1. Greater transparency in the manner in which banks fix lending rates
2. Faster transmission of policy-rate changes to borrowers
3. Complete abolition of bank-specific lending benchmarks
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: MCLR aimed to improve transparency and speed up monetary-policy transmission. It remained an internal benchmark calculated by each bank, so statement 3 is false.
82.tq: Accept the stated objectives but reject the overstatement that the framework abolished bank-specific benchmarks.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: MCLR was introduced on
82.x: The Marginal Cost of Funds-based Lending Rate system was introduced on 1 April 2016.
82.tq: Test the close dates of successive lending-rate benchmark reforms.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: From 1 October 2019, new floating-rate personal, retail and micro, small and medium enterprise loans were required to be linked to
o: an external benchmark such as the repo rate or specified Treasury-bill yield
the BPLR fixed by the RBI
the average call money rate of the preceding financial year
an internal benchmark selected by the borrowing customer
82.x: From 1 October 2019, such loans had to be linked to an external benchmark, including the repo rate, the three- or six-month Treasury-bill yield, or an FBIL-published rate.
82.tq: Apply the external-benchmark rule to the specified category of floating-rate loans.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: Which of the following is NOT an eligible external benchmark specified for the relevant floating-rate loans?
82.x: Eligible external benchmarks include the repo rate, three-month or six-month Treasury-bill yields, and an FBIL-published rate. MCLR is an internal bank benchmark, not an external benchmark.
82.tq: Find the internal benchmark hidden among externally observable reference rates.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the External Benchmark Lending Rate (EBLR) system?
o: It permits every bank to choose an entirely opaque internal rate for new floating-rate retail loans.
It links specified new floating-rate loans to an external benchmark, thereby strengthening transmission of policy rates.
It applies only to overnight inter-bank lending.
It requires the RBI to calculate each bank's operating cost and tenor premium.
82.x: EBLR links specified new floating-rate personal, retail and MSME loans to an external benchmark, improving transparency and policy transmission.
82.tq: Identify the operational consequence of replacing an internal benchmark with an external reference rate.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: MCLR — rate fixed by the MPC
TREPS — rate fixed by the Finance Ministry
T-bill yield — rate prescribed by individual commercial banks
82.x: The call money rate is market-determined. TREPS rates and Treasury-bill yields are also market-determined, whereas MCLR is calculated by each bank.
82.tq: Classify instruments by whether their rates emerge from the market, a bank or the RBI.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s:
Consider the following statements about the determination of monetary and lending rates:
1. The RBI fixes CRR and SLR.
2. Each bank computes its own MCLR.
3. The call money rate is determined by market conditions.
4. The RBI fixes the MCLR separately for every commercial bank.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: CRR and SLR are RBI-set requirements, MCLR is computed internally by each bank, and the call money rate is market-determined. Statement 4 is false.
82.tq: Use the authority distinction to detect the wrongly assigned power over MCLR.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: HDFC Bank's reported increase of its MCLR by up to 10 basis points on 8 June 2026 took its one-year MCLR to
82.x: The reported increase took HDFC Bank's one-year MCLR to 8.40%.
82.tq: Test the exact numerical outcome rather than the size of the rate change alone.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: The draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026, proposed to take effect from
82.x: The draft directions proposed an effective date of 1 April 2027.
82.tq: Distinguish the proposed implementation date from the year of issuance.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s:
Which of the following entities are covered by the draft RBI (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026?
1. Banks
2. Regional Rural Banks
3. Co-operative banks
4. All-India Financial Institutions
5. NBFCs and HFCs
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: The draft directions cover banks, RRBs, co-operative banks, AIFIs and NBFCs/HFCs.
82.tq: Treat the question as a complete institutional-coverage list and verify each category.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: Under the proposed 2026 directions, floating-rate personal and MSME loans would continue to be linked to an external benchmark and interest would be calculated on the
o: fixed original principal throughout the tenure
82.x: The proposed directions retain external-benchmark linkage for floating-rate personal and MSME loans and provide for interest on the daily reducing balance.
82.tq: Apply both conditions in the proposal instead of selecting only the benchmark-linkage feature.
82.sec: Which rates RBI fixes vs market- or bank-determined (PLR, MCLR, EBLR, call rate)  [APPSC]

82.s: Which of the following best distinguishes the Base Rate system from the MCLR system?
o: Base Rate used average cost of funds, whereas MCLR uses marginal cost of funds
Base Rate used marginal cost of funds, whereas MCLR used average cost of funds
Base Rate is applicable only to government securities, whereas MCLR applies only to deposits
Both Base Rate and MCLR are directly linked to the repo rate
82.x: The Base Rate was based on the average cost of funds and therefore transmitted policy changes slowly. MCLR uses marginal cost components, including marginal deposit costs, CRR/SLR carry, operating cost and tenor premium.
82.tq: Discriminate between two closely related benchmark-rate systems by their cost-of-funds basis.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s: Which one of the following represents the fastest route of monetary-policy transmission to lending rates?
o: Loans linked to fixed small-savings rates
Loans linked to the Base Rate
82.x: EBLR links lending rates directly to an external benchmark such as the repo rate, allowing loans to reprice more quickly than Base Rate or MCLR loans.
82.tq: Identify the institutional mechanism that transmits a policy-rate change most directly.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the components of MCLR:
1. Marginal cost of deposits is considered in MCLR.
2. CRR/SLR carry is considered in MCLR.
3. Tenor premium is considered in MCLR.
4. MCLR excludes operating cost entirely.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: MCLR incorporates marginal deposit cost, CRR/SLR carry, operating cost and tenor premium. Therefore, statement 4 is false.
82.tq: Find the single incorrect component in a list of closely related technical elements.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s: A monetary-policy stance which indicates that rates may move either upwards or downwards depending on incoming data is called:
82.x: A neutral stance means that policy rates can move in either direction and will be determined by economic data.
82.tq: Match the precise policy-stance term with its defining meaning.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s: Which one of the following correctly describes an accommodative monetary-policy stance?
o: It indicates a bias towards tightening because of excess demand
It permits only measured rate hikes at every policy meeting
It focuses exclusively on reducing inflation through liquidity absorption
It supports growth through ample liquidity and makes rate cuts more likely
82.x: An accommodative stance supports economic growth, generally provides ample liquidity and makes rate cuts more likely.
82.tq: Use the policy objective and liquidity direction to distinguish an accommodative stance from a tightening stance.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. A hawkish stance reflects concern about inflation.
2. A dovish stance reflects concern about weak growth.
3. Calibrated tightening means that rate hikes are measured and need not occur at every meeting.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: All three statements are correct. Hawkish policy prioritises inflation control, dovish policy is biased towards easing because of growth concerns, and calibrated tightening involves measured rather than automatic hikes.
82.tq: Combine related definitions and select the option containing all correctly stated policy features.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s:
Arrange the following changes in the monetary-policy stance in chronological order:
A. Neutral stance retained through August 2026
B. Return to neutral stance in June 2025
C. Shift from neutral to accommodative stance in April 2025
82.x: The stance moved from neutral to accommodative in April 2025, returned to neutral in June 2025 and remained neutral through August 2026.
82.tq: Use the dates to establish the policy-stance sequence from earliest to latest.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s: According to the policy-rate position of August 2026, which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
82.x: In August 2026, the repo rate was 5.25 per cent. The SDF was 5.00 per cent, MSF was 5.50 per cent and CRR was 3 per cent.
82.tq: Start with the sure rate-value pair and eliminate values belonging to neighbouring instruments.
82.sec: Policy rates to track - latest and past levels

82.s: The repo rate, SDF, MSF and CRR in August 2026 were respectively:
82.x: The August 2026 levels were repo 5.25 per cent, SDF 5.00 per cent, MSF 5.50 per cent and CRR 3 per cent.
82.tq: Match a group of policy instruments with their contemporaneous numerical values.
82.sec: Policy rates to track - latest and past levels

82.s: Which one of the following pairs is NOT correctly matched regarding earlier policy-rate levels?
o: Repo rate after the 2022–24 hikes — 6.5 per cent
Repo rate in April 2025 — 6.0 per cent
82.x: The MSF in April 2025 was 6.25 per cent, not 5.50 per cent. The other three pairs are correctly matched.
82.tq: Check each numerical pair against the neighbouring rate values and identify the swapped figure.
82.sec: Policy rates to track - latest and past levels

82.s: The reduction in CRR from 4 per cent before the 2025 cuts to 3 per cent in August 2026 represents a reduction of:
82.x: The CRR declined by 1 percentage point, which is equal to 100 basis points.
82.tq: Convert a percentage-point change into basis points.
82.sec: Policy rates to track - latest and past levels

82.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the SLR is correct?
o: It was 18 per cent in September 2023, compared with 38.5 per cent in 1991–92
It was 38.5 per cent in September 2023, compared with 18 per cent in 1991–92
It declined from 18 per cent in 1991–92 to 3 per cent in September 2023
It remained unchanged at 18 per cent between 1991–92 and September 2023
82.x: The SLR was recorded as 18 per cent in September 2023, whereas it had been 38.5 per cent in 1991–92.
82.tq: Test a two-period comparison by checking both the figures and their chronological placement.
82.sec: Policy rates to track - latest and past levels

82.s: Under the Flexible Inflation Targeting framework, the repo rate is best described as:
o: A fiscal borrowing rate fixed by the Finance Commission
The single operating policy rate and the most-watched monetary-policy signal
A rate used only for foreign-exchange intervention
A supplementary reserve requirement applicable to banks
82.x: Under FIT, the repo rate functions as the single operating policy rate and is the most closely watched signal of monetary policy.
82.tq: Identify the principal operating signal within the stated monetary-policy framework.
82.sec: Most powerful / widely used tool debate

82.s: Which one of the following is a limitation common to demand-side monetary-policy tools?
o: They cannot address supply-driven food or fuel inflation directly
They directly determine government tax collections
82.x: Monetary-policy tools influence demand and liquidity but cannot directly resolve inflation caused by supply disruptions in food or fuel.
82.tq: Apply the demand-side nature of monetary policy to a supply-shock situation.
82.sec: Most powerful / widely used tool debate

82.s: Sterilisation by the Reserve Bank of India refers to:
o: Increasing currency circulation after a fall in exports
Absorbing or offsetting excess rupee liquidity created by foreign-exchange inflows
Replacing open market operations with fiscal expenditure
Converting all foreign-exchange reserves into gold
82.x: When foreign-exchange inflows increase rupee liquidity, the RBI may sell government securities or conduct liquidity-absorption operations to offset the impact. This process is called sterilisation.
82.tq: Identify the policy operation by linking foreign-exchange inflows with offsetting domestic liquidity action.
82.sec: Sterilisation and instrument classification

82.s:
Which of the following are instruments that may be used for sterilising excess liquidity caused by foreign-exchange inflows?
1. Sale of government securities through OMO or MSS
2. Variable Rate Reverse Repo operations
3. Mandatory increase in government expenditure
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: The RBI may sell government securities through OMO or MSS and conduct VRRR operations to absorb excess liquidity. Increasing government expenditure is not a sterilisation instrument.
82.tq: Separate monetary-liquidity absorption tools from a fiscal expenditure measure.
82.sec: Sterilisation and instrument classification

82.s: A USD/INR buy-sell swap conducted by the RBI, such as a 3-year swap of $5 billion in December 2025, primarily:
o: Directly fixes the yield on all government securities
Injects rupee liquidity without changing the size of the RBI's balance sheet
Raises the CRR without affecting market liquidity
Absorbs rupee liquidity and permanently reduces foreign-exchange reserves
82.x: The specified buy-sell swap injects rupee liquidity while not changing the size of the RBI's balance sheet.
82.tq: Identify the liquidity and balance-sheet effect of a central-bank foreign-exchange swap.
82.sec: Sterilisation and instrument classification

82.s: The FCNR(B) inflows referred to in the September 2026 sterilisation context amounted to:
82.x: The stated FCNR(B) inflows amounted to $127.23 billion and created a situation requiring liquidity sterilisation.
82.tq: Read the scale and decimal placement carefully in a high-value financial figure.
82.sec: Sterilisation and instrument classification

82.s:
Which of the following factors influence Indian government-security yields?
1. Actions of the US Federal Reserve
2. Actions of the Reserve Bank of India
3. Inflation and short-term interest rates
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: Indian G-sec yields are influenced by all three factors: US Federal Reserve actions, RBI actions, and domestic inflation and short-term interest rates.
82.tq: Recognise that bond yields reflect both domestic monetary conditions and external financial conditions.
82.sec: Bond market and yield curve - what moves G-sec yields

82.s: The RBI's purchase of government securities worth ₹1 lakh crore in December 2025 was intended primarily to:
o: Raise the cost of government borrowing
Reduce the stock of foreign-exchange reserves
82.x: The OMO purchases of ₹1 lakh crore were intended to stabilise bond yields and support orderly financial-market conditions.
82.tq: Link the stated open-market action with its immediate bond-market objective.
82.sec: Bond market and yield curve - what moves G-sec yields

82.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the effect of a narrowing spread between Indian sovereign yields and US bond yields?
o: It necessarily depreciates the Indian rupee
It eliminates the need for domestic bond issuance
82.x: A narrower spread between Indian sovereign yields and US bond yields reduces the relative cost of borrowing for India.
82.tq: Apply the meaning of a sovereign-yield spread to borrowing costs.
82.sec: Bond market and yield curve - what moves G-sec yields

82.s:
A reduction in the repo rate can influence aggregate demand through which of the following channels?
1. Interest-rate channel
2. Credit channel
3. Exchange-rate channel
4. Asset-price channel
5. Expectations channel
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: All five are recognised transmission channels. A rate cut can lower borrowing costs, increase bank lending, weaken the currency, raise asset prices and influence inflation expectations.
82.tq: Use the complete transmission-channel classification rather than selecting only the traditional interest-rate channel.
82.sec: Transmission channels - interest rate, credit, exchange rate, asset price, expectations

82.s: Which one of the following is correctly matched with the interest-rate channel of monetary transmission?
o: Lower rates — cheaper loans leading to higher consumption and investment
Lower rates — reduced bank funds and lower lending
Lower rates — lower bond prices and a negative wealth effect
Lower rates — automatic increase in tax collection
82.x: Through the interest-rate channel, lower borrowing costs can raise consumption and investment expenditure.
82.tq: Match the channel with its direct economic mechanism rather than with an unrelated fiscal effect.
82.sec: Transmission channels - interest rate, credit, exchange rate, asset price, expectations

82.s: Which of the following statements regarding monetary transmission is correct?
o: A repo-rate change first affects money-market rates, which can affect aggregate demand and then inflation
A repo-rate cut necessarily raises household savings
A repo-rate change directly fixes agricultural output before affecting financial markets
A repo-rate cut directly increases tax collection
82.x: The transmission mechanism proceeds from the repo rate to money-market rates, then to aggregate demand and ultimately to inflation. A rate cut does not necessarily raise savings or tax collection.
82.tq: Trace the causal chain in the correct order from policy rate to inflation.
82.sec: Transmission channels - interest rate, credit, exchange rate, asset price, expectations

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Exchange-rate channel — lower rates can weaken the rupee and support exports
Asset-price channel — higher bond and equity prices can create a wealth effect
Expectations channel — a credible target necessarily removes all uncertainty about inflation
Credit channel — greater bank funds and increased lending
82.x: A credible target anchors inflation expectations; it does not necessarily remove all uncertainty. The other three channel descriptions are correct.
82.tq: Find the overstatement in an otherwise accurate list of transmission-channel effects.
82.sec: Transmission channels - interest rate, credit, exchange rate, asset price, expectations

82.s: Since February 2025, the cumulative repo-rate cuts referred to in the transmission data amounted to:
82.x: The cumulative repo-rate reduction since February 2025 was 125 basis points.
82.tq: Identify the stated cumulative policy-rate movement in basis points.
82.sec: Transmission lags - policy rate to deposit and lending rates

82.s: In September 2025, the WALR was 8.5 per cent on fresh rupee loans and 9.26 per cent on outstanding loans. The difference was:
82.x: The difference is 9.26 minus 8.50, equal to 0.76 percentage point.
82.tq: Calculate the spread between fresh-loan and outstanding-loan lending rates.
82.sec: Transmission lags - policy rate to deposit and lending rates

82.s: Why do interest rates on outstanding MCLR-linked loans generally respond more slowly than rates on EBLR-linked loans?
o: MCLR-linked loans reset only periodically, whereas EBLR-linked loans reprice quickly
MCLR-linked loans are unrelated to bank funding costs
Outstanding loans are excluded from monetary transmission
EBLR-linked loans are reset only once a year by law
82.x: MCLR-linked loans reset at periodic intervals, creating a lag. EBLR-linked loans are directly linked to an external benchmark and reprice more quickly.
82.tq: Discriminate between periodic reset behaviour and rapid external-benchmark repricing.
82.sec: Transmission lags - policy rate to deposit and lending rates

82.s: The Economic Survey described the fall in WALR on fresh loans during FY26 as a robust pass-through of:
82.x: The FY26 data cited a 64-basis-point fall in WALR on fresh loans, described as robust pass-through. A separate budget note cited 69 basis points.
82.tq: Distinguish the principal reported figure from a separately cited alternative estimate.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s:
Which of the following is an obstacle to monetary transmission in India?
1. Administered small-savings rates can keep deposit rates elevated.
2. Heavy government borrowing can keep yields high.
3. Dependence on deposits may cause banks to reprice only new deposits.
4. Informal credit markets remain outside the full reach of RBI policy.
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
82.x: All four conditions can obstruct transmission by keeping funding costs or market yields high, limiting repricing, or placing credit activity outside the formal monetary-policy channel.
82.tq: Identify all structural and market-based impediments in a multi-statement question.
82.sec: Obstacles to transmission

82.s: Which one of the following is correctly associated with the condition of banks' balance sheets and monetary transmission?
o: NPAs affect only the foreign-exchange channel
NPAs and weak balance sheets can obstruct transmission even when GNPA has fallen to a multi-decadal low
A fall in GNPA automatically eliminates every transmission obstacle
Weak balance sheets always cause an immediate fall in lending rates
82.x: NPAs and weak balance sheets can weaken transmission. GNPA was nevertheless reported at a multi-decadal low of 2.2 per cent in September 2025.
82.tq: Avoid the absolute claim that an improvement in one indicator removes all structural constraints.
82.sec: Obstacles to transmission

82.s: The GNPA ratio cited for September 2025 was:
82.x: Gross non-performing assets were reported at a multi-decadal low of 2.2 per cent in September 2025.
82.tq: Read the decimal placement correctly in a banking-sector ratio.
82.sec: Obstacles to transmission

82.s: Which one of the following is NOT identified as an obstacle to monetary transmission?
o: A permanent elimination of government borrowing from the bond market
Liquidity mismatches in the banking system
Preference for cash and the presence of an unorganised money market
82.x: Government borrowing remains a factor that can keep yields high; its permanent elimination is not an identified obstacle or feature of the system.
82.tq: Reject the option that introduces an unsupported absolute condition while retaining the genuine obstacles.
82.sec: Obstacles to transmission

82.s: Which statement best describes the relationship between liquidity conditions and monetary transmission?
o: Surplus liquidity generally pulls market rates below the repo rate and speeds up transmission
Deficit liquidity strengthens transmission by restricting bank funds
Surplus liquidity always pushes market rates above the repo rate
Liquidity conditions have no effect on money-market rates
82.x: Surplus liquidity can lower market rates below the repo rate and facilitate transmission. Deficit liquidity tends to weaken transmission.
82.tq: Compare surplus and deficit liquidity by their effects on market rates and transmission strength.
82.sec: Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit

82.s: In December 2025, the RBI responded to tighter liquidity caused by currency leakage, tax outflows and reserve needs through:
o: ₹1 lakh crore of OMO sales and a $5 billion reverse swap
₹1 lakh crore of OMO purchases and a $5 billion swap
Complete withdrawal of all liquidity operations
A 2 percentage-point increase in CRR alone
82.x: Tighter liquidity in December 2025 led the RBI to inject ₹1 lakh crore through OMO purchases along with a $5 billion swap.
82.tq: Link the stated liquidity pressures with the specific combination of remedial instruments.
82.sec: Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit

82.s: The RBI's stated intention to maintain 'sufficient liquidity' was aimed at:
o: Replacing the monetary-policy framework with fiscal policy
Preventing all future changes in the repo rate
82.x: Maintaining sufficient liquidity was intended to support and improve transmission of monetary policy to market and lending rates.
82.tq: Identify the policy objective attached to the central bank's liquidity commitment.
82.sec: Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit

82.s: By 3 September 2026, the liquidity surplus had reached approximately:
82.x: The surplus was approximately ₹10.32 lakh crore by 3 September 2026.
82.tq: Distinguish the correct Indian-numbering scale in a large liquidity figure.
82.sec: Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit

82.s: When the RBI began draining the liquidity surplus in September 2026, the instrument specifically mentioned was:
o: Emergency increase in the repo rate to 10 per cent
82.x: The RBI began absorbing the large surplus through Variable Rate Reverse Repo, or VRRR, operations.
82.tq: Match a liquidity-absorption situation with the appropriate operating instrument.
82.sec: Liquidity conditions and transmission - surplus vs deficit

82.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Credit growth was 14.5 per cent year-on-year in December 2025.
2. A rate cut increases investment expenditure through the monetary-transmission process.
3. A rate cut necessarily increases savings and tax collection.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: Credit growth was 14.5 per cent year-on-year in December 2025, and lower rates can increase investment expenditure. A rate cut does not necessarily raise savings or tax collection, making statement 3 false.
82.tq: Combine a numerical indicator with a causal statement and reject an unsupported consequence.
82.sec: Monetary transmission - MCLR, EBLR, lags, stance terms

82.s: The Internal Study Group on the working of the MCLR system, constituted by the RBI in 2017, was chaired by whom?
82.x: The RBI’s Internal Study Group on the working of the MCLR system was chaired by Janak Raj in 2017.
82.tq: Use the committee-chairperson association to identify the correct answer.
82.sec: Internal study groups on MCLR and external benchmarking  [GROUP-II]

82.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the RBI’s Internal Study Group on the MCLR system:
1. It found that transmission under the MCLR system was weak.
2. It recommended a shift to an external benchmark.
3. Its recommendations led to the EBLR mandate from 1 October 2019.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
82.x: The study group found weak MCLR transmission, recommended external benchmarking, and its recommendations led to the EBLR mandate effective from 1 October 2019.
82.tq: Check the complete policy sequence from diagnosis to recommendation and implementation.
82.sec: Internal study groups on MCLR and external benchmarking  [GROUP-II]

82.s: The External Benchmark-based Lending Rate (EBLR) mandate came into effect from:
82.x: The EBLR mandate became effective on 1 October 2019 following concerns about weak transmission under the MCLR system.
82.tq: Distinguish the implementation date from the date of the study group’s formation.
82.sec: Internal study groups on MCLR and external benchmarking  [GROUP-II]

82.s:
With reference to the monetary policy outlook in August 2026, consider the following statements:
1. The MPC minutes indicated a possibility of a policy rate hike.
2. Headline inflation had averaged 3.93 per cent so far in 2026–27.
3. Core inflation was projected at 4.3 per cent.
4. The Governor associated with this policy outlook was Sanjay Malhotra.
Which of the statements given above are correct?

4. OMO purchases of ₹1 lakh crore in December 2025.

Abolish external benchmarking and restore MCLR

82.s:
Assertion (A): The repo rate cannot by itself resolve food or fuel supply shocks.

o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

Arrange the following approaches to monetary policy in India in chronological order:

B. Monetary targeting

Adoption of CPI as the nominal anchor

Continuation of the multiple-indicator approach as the sole framework

required the MPC to meet only once every five years
excluded inflation from the policy framework

o: The RBI Governor has two votes in every meeting.

The Central Government can overrule a majority decision of the MPC.

o: Four years and are not eligible for reappointment
Two years and are eligible for unlimited reappointment
Five years and are appointed by the RBI Central Board
Three years and are eligible for one reappointment

o: The MPC must meet every month without exception.

The MPC meets only when the Finance Ministry requests it.

o: Four external members, including the Government nominee
All six members of the Committee

o: Section 45T of the RBI Act, following the 2008 amendment

Section 42 of the Banking Regulation Act, following the 1991 reforms

names of all MPC members and their individual salaries

83.s: Which one of the following correctly compares the flexibility of fiscal and monetary policy?

will always drain liquidity from the banking system

a tightening bias aimed at draining excess liquidity
a fiscal programme of increasing subsidies
a neutral position in which rates can move either way

It changed from neutral to accommodative in April 2025 after the repo rate was cut to 6 per cent, and was neutral in 2026 after the rate was held at 5.25 per cent.

NARCL is majority private and IDRCL is majority public-sector owned
